meta/architecture.md:
# Architecture & Data Model

Design blueprint for the **VeVe Collect community app** — a free tool that turns this wiki into a living product: a beautiful reference **plus** personalized tools (MCP optimizer, set tracker, floor history, holder distribution). Grounded in [[data-landscape-and-apis]], [[economy-gems-omi-mcp]], [[catalog-rarity-drops]].

> [!success] Status (2026-06-25) — prototype is live
> All three personalized tools run **live on real on-chain holdings** via `app/assets/collectscan.js` (CORS open, no proxy): **MCP Optimizer** (live daily MCP + full-catalog, set-aware "cheapest points"), **Set Tracker** (owned vs. missing per set), **Mint Checker** (significant-mint scan incl. grail years). The wiki catalog/sets are exported to `app/data/catalog.js` (1,091 collectibles, 345 sets). **The floor-price feed is now LIVE on-chain** via StackR on Base (see §6) — `app/data/floor.js`; the optimizer & set tracker use real StackR floor (falling back to drop price where unlisted). Still a static prototype (no-cache `devserver.py`); Next.js migration is future.

> [!note] Terminology (corrected from research)
> **VeVe** = the app. **Collect** = the company (ex-ECOMI) + its blockchain ("Collect Chain"). **StackR** = a *separate* marketplace (on Base) for OMI↔Gems and NFT trading — **not** a rebrand of VeVe. The app will *link to* StackR/Collect, but they are distinct.

## 1. System Overview

```
┌─────────────────────┐     build/export      ┌──────────────────────┐
│  CONTENT LAYER       │ ────────────────────► │  WEB APP (Next.js)    │
│  Obsidian wiki       │  static catalog +     │  - reference pages    │
│  (this vault)        │  set definitions +    │  - MCP optimizer      │
│  human-curated facts │  brand/universe data  │  - set tracker        │
└─────────────────────┘                       │  - floor / holders    │
                                               └─────────┬────────────┘
                                                         │ reads
                              ┌──────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┐
                              ▼                           ▼                           ▼
                   ┌────────────────────┐   ┌────────────────────────┐   ┌────────────────────┐
                   │ collectscan API     │   │ Floor / drop data       │   │ Static catalog JSON │
                   │ (Blockscout, public)│   │ (HARD GAP — see §6)     │   │ (exported from wiki)│
                   │ holders, transfers, │   │ scrape / partner /      │   │ brands, sets, items │
                   │ editions, ownership │   │ self-maintained         │   │ rarity, edition size│
                   └────────────────────┘   └────────────────────────┘   └────────────────────┘
```

Three sources, three reliability tiers:
1. **On-chain (collectscan)** — authoritative, public, free, but no floor/USD/drop data. Used for: a wallet's holdings, holder distribution, edition counts, transfer history.
2. **Floor/drop data** — the hard gap. No official or on-chain source. See §6.
3. **Static catalog** — exported from this wiki + a catalog source; the canonical list of brands, universes, collectibles, sets, rarities, edition sizes.

## 2. Identity / Auth Model

- **No VeVe account OAuth exists. No username→wallet lookup.** *(see [[data-landscape-and-apis]])*
- **Users paste their Collect Chain wallet address.** The app queries collectscan for that address. Read-only, no login, no custody, no keys.
- Optionally cache a session's wallet in localStorage. Never request private keys or seed phrases — display a clear "read-only, public on-chain data" notice.

### Future: authenticated "own wallet only" mode (roadmap)
Today anyone can paste any address (on-chain data is public anyway). Restricting to the user's *own verified* wallet becomes possible via either path, once available:
1. **Platform login (most likely)** — if VeVe / Collect / StackR exposes an OAuth / "Sign in" flow or an authenticated API (the API the owner mentioned), we use it to fetch the logged-in user's own wallet + holdings and lock the tools to it. Fits the plan to link this into the platform once complete.
2. **Wallet-connect + SIWE (crypto-native)** — once VeVe ships **self-custody (Phase 2, announced not live)**, the user connects their wallet (WalletConnect) and signs a Sign-In-With-Ethereum message to *prove* ownership; we then restrict to that verified address.

Note: "own wallet only" is a UX/trust feature, not a privacy one — on-chain holdings are public regardless. It matters most if we ever add write-actions or account-specific data beyond on-chain.

## 3. Data Model (canonical schemas)

TypeScript-style; the app's `types/` mirrors these. Filled fields come from the wiki; live fields from collectscan; floor fields from §6.

```ts
type Universe   = { slug: string; name: string; licensor?: string; parent?: string; flag?: string }  // wiki domains/
type Brand      = { slug: string; name: string; universe: string; licensor?: string }                // wiki entities/
type Collectible = {
  id: string;                 // VeVe collectible id (catalog)
  name: string; brand: string; universe: string;
  format: 'collectible' | 'comic' | 'art';
  rarity: 'Common'|'Uncommon'|'Rare'|'Ultra Rare'|'Secret Rare';
  editionSize: number;        // total minted
  setId?: string;             // membership in a Set
  dropDate?: string;          // §6 gap
  image?: string;
}
type Edition    = { collectibleId: string; mintNumber: number; owner: string }   // on-chain (collectscan instances)
type Holding    = { collectibleId: string; mintNumber: number; rarity: string; format: string }  // a wallet's owned editions
type FloorPoint = { collectibleId: string; ts: string; floorGems: number }       // §6 time series
type HolderDist = { collectibleId: string; uniqueHolders: number; buckets: {min:number;max:number;count:number}[] }
type GameSet    = { id: string; name: string; brand: string; memberCollectibleIds: string[] }  // a "Set" for completion
```

## 4. Feature Spec — Set Tracker ("what am I missing")

> "Master set" = a **Set** completed under the Master Collector Program. We use "set".

1. Input: wallet address (+ optional brand/universe filter, e.g. "Star Wars").
2. Fetch holdings: collectscan → wallet's owned collectibleIds + mint numbers.
3. Load set definitions from the static catalog (`GameSet[]`).
4. For each set in scope: compute `owned ∩ members` vs `members` → **owned / missing / % complete**.
5. UI: per-set progress bars, grid of owned (lit) vs missing (dimmed), "missing" list with floor price (if available) and a buy link to VeVe/StackR.
6. Rewards context: show the **+100 one-off** + daily set points (1.0–5.0 by size) that completing the set would yield (from the MCP rules).

## 5. Feature Spec — MCP Optimizer ("cheapest Master Collector Points")

The killer feature. **The MCP formula is public** ([[Master Collector Points]]), so the math is exact; only the *price* side needs floor data.

1. Input: wallet address (holdings) → optionally a goal (raise rank / +X daily points / complete a set).
2. Compute **current daily Asset Points** from holdings using the canonical formula (§ MCP rules below).
3. Generate **candidate acquisitions** from the catalog (items the user doesn't have, or duplicates that still pay).
4. For each candidate compute **marginal daily points** Δ (respecting rarity bonus, low-mint, duplicate diminishing, and set-completion thresholds) and **cost in Gems** (floor price).
5. Rank by **points-per-Gem (Δpoints / costGems)** → "cheapest points" list. Highlight set-completion synergies (a cheap item that finishes a set unlocks +100 + daily set points).
6. Factor holdings: duplicates the user already owns get diminished Δ; near-complete sets get boosted Δ.
7. Output: ranked recommendations + projected new daily total + projected rank movement (qualitative — exact rank thresholds aren't public).

### MCP rules (canonical — implement exactly; source [[economy-gems-omi-mcp]])

```
COLLECTIBLE daily base = 1.0
  rarity bonus (added): Rare +0.25, Ultra Rare +0.50, Secret Rare +5.00   (Common/Uncommon +0)
  low-mint bonus: +0.5 if mint in lowest 5% of edition
  duplicate factor by copy index: 1st 1.00, 2nd 0.75, 3rd 0.35, 4th+ 0.10

COMIC daily base by rarity = {Common 0.25, Uncommon 0.50, Rare 2.0, Ultra Rare 3.0, Secret Rare 6.0}
  low-mint bonus: +50% if mint in lowest 5%
  duplicate factor: 1st 1.00, 2nd 0.50, 3rd 0.25, 4th+ 0.10   (Common & Uncommon comics EXEMPT → always 1.00)
  NO set bonus for comics

SET completion daily by set size = {1:1.0, 2:2.0, 3:3.0, 4:4.0, 5+:5.0}
  duplicate-set factor: 1st 1.00, 2nd 0.30, 3rd 0.20, 4th+ 0.10

ONE-OFF: onboarding +100; complete a set +100 (once ever); store buy +25; market buy +15
DAILY ACTIVITY: +1 per action, cap 25/day
OMI REWARD TIER: bonus daily ∝ OMI held (max 10M eligible)   [formula not fully public]

RANKS: 22, Starter → Master Collector (top ~3%), percentile-based, dynamic
LEVELS: 0–100, permanent, exponential   [exact thresholds NOT public — do not invent]
```

> [!warning] Don't overpromise
> Exact **Level thresholds** and the **OMI reward curve** are not public. The optimizer gives exact *daily points* and *points-per-Gem*, but rank/level projections must be **qualitative** ("this likely moves you up"), never a fake precise number.

## 6. The Floor / Drop Data Gap — SOLVED (StackR on-chain, 2026-06-25)

> [!success] Floor feed is live and on-chain — no scrape, no partner, no ToS risk
> VeVe's **primary**-market floor isn't on-chain (gas-free internal transfers carry no price; the VeVe GraphQL is CSRF/auth-gated). **But the StackR secondary market IS fully on-chain on Base** and free to read. Verified contract **`StackrListings` `0x5ccdcd1592cf055ae08e35f948f7627473c55432`** emits `ItemListed(listingId, …, tokenId, …, price, payToken, …)` / `ItemBought` / `ItemCanceled` / `ItemReleased`. We read these from the free **`base.blockscout.com`** Blockscout API (pre-decoded logs), reconcile **active** listings (Listed − Bought/Canceled/Released by listingId), map each VeVe `tokenId → collectible name` via collectscan instance metadata, and convert **OMI → USD** (1 Gem = $1). Floor per collectible = **min active StackR listing**.

**Implementation:** `/tmp/gen_floor.py` (the indexer) writes **`app/data/floor.js`** = `window.FLOOR { asOf, omiUsd, source, byName:{name:{omi,usd,listings}} }` — a refreshable on-chain snapshot, exactly like the wiki→`catalog.js` export. The app joins it by collectible name (exact, then normalized) and uses it as **real acquisition cost** in the MCP Optimizer (cost = live StackR floor where listed, else original drop price, clearly labeled ⛓ vs ~) and the Set Tracker (portfolio value + cost-to-complete-a-set). Re-run `gen_floor.py` to refresh.

**Honest limits:** (1) it's the **StackR secondary** floor, not VeVe's primary store price; (2) coverage = items currently *listed* on StackR (the rest fall back to drop price); (3) name-join misses where the catalog title is embellished vs the canonical VeVe name; (4) reconciliation is windowed (a snapshot, not a real-time index). All labeled in-app with an "as of" date.

Earlier-considered alternatives (now unnecessary): partner feed (Veve Alpha/EcomiWiki — SPAs, Cloudflare-gated), VeVe GraphQL (CSRF/auth-gated), community crowd-sourcing, user-entered (kept as a possible future manual override).

## 7. Tech Stack (recommended)

- **Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind** — SSR/ISR for fast reference pages, API routes to proxy+cache collectscan (hide rate limits, add our own caching), one deployable unit. Deploy on **Vercel** (or Cloudflare).
- **Caching:** a thin server cache (KV / edge cache) in front of collectscan — never hammer it from the browser. Respect undocumented limits.
- **Content pipeline:** a build step exports the wiki's brand/universe/set facts (frontmatter + a catalog JSON) into the app's `data/`.
- **Prototype now:** static, dependency-light app in `app/` (mock data + the real MCP formula) that migrates cleanly to the Next.js target. See `app/README.md`.

## 8. Roadmap

1. **Now:** prototypes on mock data (set tracker + MCP optimizer with real formula); architecture (this doc); deepen wiki content.
2. **Next:** wire collectscan API (holdings, holder distribution, editions) behind a cached proxy; wallet-paste flow.
3. **Then:** solve the floor-data gap (§6); historical floor charts.
4. **Later:** export the full catalog/sets from the wiki; polish reference pages; link from StackR/Collect to launch as the community gift.

## Open questions for the owner
- Floor-data source (§6) — partner, self-scrape, or user-entered?
- Confirm "Set completion" definition per set (per-collectible vs per-rarity) — affects the tracker.
- Is there an API you have access to (you mentioned one)? If so it may replace/augment collectscan.

meta/conventions.md:
# Conventions

How this wiki is organized and maintained.

## Folder Map

```
.raw/                 source documents — immutable, never edited
wiki/
├── index.md          master catalog (update on every ingest)
├── overview.md       executive summary / front door
├── hot.md            ~500-word recent-context cache
├── log.md            append-only operation log (newest at top)
├── domains/          top-level topic hubs
├── entities/         people, companies, brands, notable collectibles
├── concepts/         mechanics, ideas, terminology
├── sources/          one summary per ingested source
├── comparisons/      side-by-side analyses
├── questions/        filed answers to good questions
└── meta/             glossary, conventions, dashboards
_templates/           Obsidian Templater note templates
```

## Page Rules

- Every page uses YAML frontmatter: `type`, `status`, `created`, `updated`, `tags` (minimum).
- Links use `[[Page Name]]` wikilinks — filenames are unique, no paths needed.
- `status` values: `seed` (stub) → `developing` → `mature`.
- New pages start as `seed` and graduate as cited facts are added.

## Accuracy Policy

This is a **public** wiki, so facts must be trustworthy.

- High-level, durable facts can be stated directly.
- Anything **volatile or uncertain** (prices, token economics, exact mechanics, current brand roster, app features that change) is flagged **(to verify)** or in a `> [!warning]` callout until backed by a dated, cited source.
- Never invent specific numbers. Cite the source and timestamp the figure.
- `.raw/` sources are never modified.

## Maintenance

- Update [[index]], the relevant `_index`, [[log]], and [[hot]] on every change.
- Run *"lint the wiki"* every ~10–15 ingests to catch orphans, dead links, and stale claims.

meta/daily-ingest.md:
# Daily New-Drops Ingest

A daily job pulls **new VeVe drops** (collectibles + comic covers) from the Collect Chain on-chain feed into the wiki + app data. No manual step needed.

## What runs

- **Scheduler:** a macOS **LaunchAgent** — `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.veve.wiki.dailyingest.plist` — fires **daily at 10:00**.
- **Wrapper:** `tools/daily_ingest.sh` → runs `tools/ingest_new_drops.py --write` with `TODAY`/`PAGES`, logs to `tools/ingest.log`.
- **Ingest:** `tools/ingest_new_drops.py` — idempotent on-chain watcher (`collectscan.com/api/v2/tokens/<contract>/instances`, newest-first). For each drop **not already in the wiki** (dedup by name+rarity / name+issue, token-containment vs embellished titles) it captures the **full on-chain metadata**:
  - **Collectibles →** new `wiki/collectibles/*.md` page: Overview from the on-chain **description**, `rarity`, `edition_size`, `nft_drop_date`, `set` (series), `edition_type: FE` when First Edition, and a 🔑 **first-appearance** tag + callout when the description flags one. (`season` is **not** on-chain — VeVe-DB only — so new pages have no season until the next CSV export; see [[../log|log]] (v).)
  - **Comics →** appended to `app/data/comics.js` with real **publication year** (`startYear`, not the drop date), **Age** (Golden…Modern via `tools/comic_ages.py`), 🔑 **first-appearance**, publisher, rarities, edition, floor.
- **Then regenerates:** `export_catalog.py` (→ `catalog.js`) + `gen_notable_mints.py`.

## Check / control

```sh
launchctl list | grep veve            # registered? (col 2 = last exit code, 0 = ok)
tail -n 40 "tools/ingest.log"         # what the last runs did
bash tools/daily_ingest.sh            # run once now (manual)
launchctl start com.veve.wiki.dailyingest   # trigger the agent now
launchctl unload -w ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.veve.wiki.dailyingest.plist   # disable
launchctl load   -w ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.veve.wiki.dailyingest.plist   # re-enable
```

- **Deploy to the demo:** off by default (outward-facing). Set `DEPLOY=1` in the wrapper (or run `DEPLOY=1 bash tools/daily_ingest.sh`) to also push `app/` to the GitHub Pages demo after ingest.
- **Full Disk Access caveat:** `export_catalog.py` reads the authoritative CSV in `~/Downloads`. macOS may block a background (launchd) process from `~/Downloads`; the ingest handles this gracefully (the CSV join for image/blind-box/series is skipped, everything else still runs). To enable the join under launchd, grant Full Disk Access to `/bin/bash` (or `/usr/bin/python3`) in System Settings → Privacy & Security.

> [!note] Strict accuracy
> On-chain metadata only — nothing invented. New pages are `confidence: high`, `status: developing`, with `veve_url`/`collect_url` left `# TODO`. LLM enrichment (deepened About, researched character first-appearance years) is a separate, on-request pass — not part of the unattended daily job.

fm.title: Held-back vs unsold vs burnt — methodology

meta/held-back.md:
# Held back vs unsold vs burnt

VeVe keeps editions out of collectors' hands in **three distinct ways** — they are NOT the same thing:

| | What it is | How we know it |
|---|---|---|
| 🔒 **Held back** | **Reserved low mints** — #1 up to the lowest *public* mint. VeVe withholds these permanently; they were never for sale. | `lowest_public_mint` → reserve = `lowmint − 1`. On-chain they sit in the **reserve wallet** (below). |
| 📦 **Unsold** | Editions that **didn't sell** — still in VeVe's Store (or later burnt). | `collectible_available` (CSV) → catalog `store`. |
| 🔥 **Burnt** | Editions **removed from supply** (e.g. the 2026 Street Fighter burn). | `collectible_editions_burnt` (CSV) → catalog `burnt`. On-chain in the **burn wallet**. |

The key rule (per owner): **anything below a collectible's lowest-public mint is held back for certain.** At/above it, an edition is with a collector, unsold, or burnt.

## On-chain wallets (verified)

The VeVe contract is `0xbcFEbA7A9dA14f5C9453bDA72E2098537867B3c7`. Its two largest holders are distinct:

- 🔥 **Burn / unsold wallet — `0x39E3816A8C549Ec22Cd1a34a8CF7034B3941d8B1`** (~1.45M editions). Holds **high, scattered mints** of undersold drops (e.g. Sakura - Battle at #38, #302, #564). Its size ≈ CSV unsold (611k) + burnt (676k). This is where burnt/unsold editions go — **not** the reserve.
- 🔒 **Reserve / custody wallet — `0x7be178ba43a9828C22997a3EC3640497d88D2fd3`** (~517k editions). Holds the **reserved low mints** — verified holding systematic #1-onward ranges (Katara #1–10, Pink Floyd #1–10, IG-11 #1, Assassin's Creed #1–10) plus VeVe event-award / operational items.

**Verification method:** a collectible's reserved editions are the mints *below* its lowest-public mint; those sit in the reserve wallet `0x7be1…`. The burn wallet's mints are high/scattered (unsold that got burnt).

> [!warning] What we can and can't pinpoint
> - **Held back (below lowest-public):** exact and certain from `lowest_public_mint` — no on-chain call needed.
> - **A specific circulating edition's owner** (e.g. "who owns #1987?"): **not** derivable from our data. VeVe token IDs are not sequential per collectible (can't compute a token's ID from its edition #), and collectscan can't map (collectible, edition) → owner. Getting the exact holder needs VeVe's own app or a full ~6M-instance owner index. We answer the certain part (reserve) and give the burnt/unsold **counts** for the rest.

## Ask it
[Ask the Wiki](../../app/ask.html) answers all of these live, and includes an **edition locator**:
- *"which Disney collectibles are held back?"* → reserved low mints (`reserve = lowmint − 1`).
- *"which Marvel collectibles were burnt?"* → `burnt` counts. *"…unsold?"* → `store` counts.
- *"where is #5 of Katara - Water Master?"* → **🔒 Held back** (below the lowest public mint #6).
- *"where is #1987 of S3LF MADE?"* → **❔ no such edition** (only 250 minted).

> [!note] Snapshot
> `store`/`issued`/`burnt` come from the Collect Chain export (2026-06-26) and shift over time; a fresh export refreshes them. Reserve = researched `lowest_public_mint`.

meta/reserve-first-public-mint.md:
# First-Public-Mint (Reserve) Backfill

The Mint Checker's "🥇 THE lowest public mint" and "top-5 lowest available" flags need each collectible's **first public mint** = `reserve_count + 1` (VeVe withholds `#1..N`). This page records why it isn't auto-derivable and the authoritative one-query fix.

## Why it can't be derived from what we have (verified 2026-06-27)

- **DB export (CSVs):** no reserve/withheld field; `available`/`store_allocation` are current-state, not the drop reserve.
- **Edition size:** does NOT correlate — reserve-40 and reserve-20 are mixed across *every* edition tier (only edition ≥8000 is reliably 40). A guess would mislabel #21 vs #41.
- **collectscan (on-chain):** the reserved low mints sit in the **`VeveCollection`** wallet (`0x7be1…2fd3`) as **bare pre-mints — null metadata, null image, no id** → unidentifiable; and the API can't enumerate one collectible's instances by name. (Storage wallets that *do* carry metadata — CollectionStorage/Parking — hold high/mid editions, not the low reserves.)
- **VeVe blog:** collectible pages are JS-rendered SPAs and our slugs don't map → not scrapable.

Result: only **~340 items** have a researched `lowest_public_mint` (wired into the app already). The other ~1,600 need the source below.

## The authoritative fix — one query on the Collect warehouse

The warehouse (where `patrick_taxonomy_*` came from) has the `nft` table: `element_id` (= a collectible_type id = our `collect_id`, or a comic_cover id), `issue` (the mint number), `owner_id`. `_veve_users.md` lists every VeVe **system** user-id. So the first public mint = the lowest `issue` whose owner is a real user:

```sql
SELECT element_id, element_type, MIN(issue) AS first_public_mint
FROM nft
WHERE owner_id NOT IN (
  '160368a8-a67d-4425-a46e-d8efc67f3c3e', -- VeveStore
  'a95e0145-dcf6-490e-9c5b-0d2987b880c4', -- VeveCollection (pre-minted reserves)
  '919668c3-4a0c-4585-8086-ec0976a9cbe4', -- VeveBurn
  '54b700bb-8700-4832-a2a8-ef03bee9fd64', -- VeVeUserBurn
  '16020975-9b7e-462d-b69a-721532b89e6a', -- VeveCraftStorage
  '78b562c6-13e3-4009-aa1e-725d7fff47ac', -- VeVeCollectionStorage
  '153bdac6-c6ce-4e0f-9142-5b47dad40a14', -- VeVeCollectionParking
  'fe97b620-d22e-4b0d-8bc6-d659da2c52ad', -- VeVeCollector1939 (Marvel comic vault)
  'f69ab9f1-1ffd-4e4e-9db3-d6718cadba96', -- VeVeAssist
  '49c36649-4cc1-497c-a5c0-897c2204e92d', -- TWDCCollectibles
  -- guest/demo accounts:
  '1f6eef87-7e48-471e-b3e0-8a7876bc6bbd','2b25632b-720a-447f-ab37-5b0a07822f9e',
  '1a6a2053-0e74-47dd-a9a3-488b2094afd1','e4deda5d-d208-4a8e-995f-6b6c80642d62',
  '0d32e73f-8f27-49b9-83b8-ce4046a3e855','2fb95a2b-3b65-4fcb-8ade-02b840e0a4af',
  '4ef5cc72-2dfc-44af-b5a6-bd6a2acee448','584fb33d-7089-451b-96da-1d48ed79186a',
  '7d38adce-db8a-45e0-ab27-afefbc6dae38','9328d32e-f7b5-4d83-adfa-3c82d926f310'
)
GROUP BY element_id, element_type;
```

Export the result as CSV (columns `element_id,first_public_mint`; `element_type` optional) to **`app/data/first_public_mint.csv`**. Then `/tmp/apply_first_public.py` joins it by `collect_id` → sets `lowest_public_mint` on every collectible and re-exports the catalog. Authoritative first-public for the **entire** catalog (and comics, via `comic_cover` ids), in one pass.

> [!note] Burn wallets are excluded too, so a low mint that was bought-then-burned doesn't masquerade as the public floor.

# Review Queue — Owner Corrections Pass

A consolidated, prioritized checklist for the human review pass. The wiki was built **iteratively at scale** (parallel research agents → generator → dedup), with a strict no-invention policy: anything unverified is `# TODO` or flagged. This page surfaces everything that wants a human eye, newest data as of **batch 7 (864 collectibles)**.

> [!tip] Fastest way to work this queue
> Open **`collectibles/collectibles.base` → the "Needs review (conf < high)" view**. Every collectible now carries a **`confidence`** frontmatter field (`high` / `medium` / `low`). That view lists only the **407** items below `high` confidence, sortable by universe. Fix a value → bump its `confidence` to `high`.

## Confidence snapshot (864 collectibles)

| Confidence | Count | Meaning |
|-----------|------:|---------|
| `high` | 457 | Verified against the authoritative VeVe blog (or 2+ sources). Trust these. |
| `medium` | 405 | Has a source note but no explicit cross-verification, **or** bulk-ingested early. Spot-check edition/price/date. |
| `low` | 2 | Explicitly uncertain — verify first. |

**Low-confidence items (verify first):**
- [[star-wars-obi-wan-haja-s1]] — Haja Estree (Obi-Wan Series 1)
- [[tmnt-leonardo]] — Leonardo

## 1. Licensor flags — ✅ RESOLVED (web-verified 2026-06-25)

Rights-holders confirmed and filled (domains + their collectibles); flux callouts updated to verified notes:

- [[domains/star-trek]] — **Paramount** / parent **Paramount Skydance Corporation** (Skydance–Paramount merger completed **7 Aug 2025**).
- [[domains/tmnt]] + [[domains/avatar-the-last-airbender]] — **Nickelodeon** / **Paramount Skydance Corporation**.

## 2. Domains missing `licensor` / `parent` — ✅ mostly resolved

Franchise **debut years** filled on all 13 stub domains (alien, astro-boy, avatar, cartoon-network, james-bond, knight-rider, labyrinth, rabbids, rambo, ren-and-stimpy, solo-leveling, ultraman, voltron). Licensor/parent filled for the flux franchises above; remaining stubs (labyrinth, knight-rider, ren-and-stimpy, solo-leveling, tarzan, etc.) carry their best-known licensor or a note.

## 3. Collectibles with `licensor: "# TODO"` — ✅ DONE (0 remain)

All 23 filled from §1: james-bond→Amazon MGM Studios (9), tmnt→Nickelodeon (6), star-trek→Paramount (4), robocop→Amazon MGM Studios (3), rambo→StudioCanal (1).

## 3b. Significant mints + content — ✅ done this pass

- **Significant-years engine** expanded to **all 34 universes** (`app/assets/significant-years.js`) — Mint Checker now flags grail years everywhere.
- **"Notable mints"** section auto-generated into **983 collectibles** (`/tmp/gen_notable_mints.py`) — each page lists its debut-year mint 🎯, universe grail mints 🏆, #1/first-public, memes, repdigits.
- **Overview** enriched on all **1,091** pages from verified data (`/tmp/gen_overview.py`) — universe context, set, edition, rarity, drop, first appearance.
- **"## About" lore on ALL 1,091 pages** (9 parallel agents → `/tmp/apply_about.py`) — 2–3 sentences of who/what it depicts + franchise significance, knowledge-grounded, no fabricated stats. Every collectible is now fully answerable.

## Per-variant edition + mislabel flags (2026-06-25 dedup/audit sweep)

- **OPN Heart** (Jason Naylor, veve-vibes 2024-11-16): ANIMATED(SR)/COLOR(UR)/BLACKOUT(UR) all show **ed 555** — SR shouldn't equal UR; verify per-variant counts.
- **Tokimondo Kaiju** (tokidoki 2023-10-13): editions don't follow the rarity curve (UR Kaiju Chameleon 1050 = Common Kaiju Tokimon 1050; Uncommon 1850 > Common 1050) — verify per-variant.
- **Sket One mislabels:** existing `sket-one-ting` should be titled **"Ting — Phase One"** and `sket-one-greaper` **"Greaper — Black Death"** (generic titles; the other variants were added in the veve-vibes audit).

## Verification flags — your call (found during the 2026-06-25 verify pass)

These were left **unchanged** because they need a judgment call (not just a value fill). Full change log of what *was* auto-corrected: `/tmp/verify_changes.log`.

- **DC "Batman: Black & White" character/title:** VeVe's official pages title **`batman-bw-s2-61-dick-sprang` = "The Joker"** and **`batman-bw-s2-72-carmine-infantino` = "Robin"**, but the wiki `character`/`title` say Batman. Decide whether to re-label (ripples to the auto-generated entity pages) or keep under the Batman B&W line.
- **Game-year drop dates (likely conflation):** some **Street Fighter** (`M. Bison`, `Sakura`, `Guile`) and **Assassin's Creed** (Eivor/Valhalla) entries have a game-release year in `nft_drop_date` and could not be confirmed as released VeVe drops — they may be erroneous entries or unreleased. Verify existence; fix or remove.
- **~30 genuinely-unverifiable items** stay `medium`: recent 2026 drops (IG-11, Yoda figure, Millennium Falcon, AT-AT S7, Edo troopers) with no indexed spec page yet, and craft-only/airdrop items with no list price.

## What's left for a future pass (not blocking)
- **86 medium-confidence** collectibles remain (down from 431): one lost batch of 56 to re-verify (process restarted mid-run) + the ~30 unverifiable above. Filter `collectibles.base` → "Needs review".
- Optionally upgrade "## About" with real VeVe blog marketing copy where it adds flavor beyond public knowledge.
- Minor licensor flags: [[entities/chucky]] (split rights), voltron/ultraman parent nuance.
- More coverage: real-world-brand long tail + the **comics corpus** (~5k, still deferred).

## 4. Judgment calls surfaced by the research agents

These are **real but ambiguous** — they need an owner decision, not just verification:

- **Disney Parks attraction posters (14 items, conf=medium):** the *Disneyland Resort Tomorrowland* (4), *Fantasyland* (5), *Disneyland Paris* (5), and *Haunted Mansion* (3) series are attraction posters/objects, not core Disney Animation. Included because they're genuine VeVe drops, but **you may want to rescope** them out of `disney` (or into a `disney-parks` universe). Only *Madame Leota* among them is a true character.
- **Vintage Metal Disney Villains posters (5):** 2D metal-poster collectibles, distinct from the existing 3D villain statues — confirmed separate series. Kept as their own items.
- **Marvel possible duplicates** to reconcile against existing bare-name entries:
  - "Captain America — Animated" / "Ultimate Animated" (Marvel 1st Cap S1, 2021) vs the list's bare "Animated"/"Ultimate Animated".
  - "Silver Surfer (SDCC 2022 statue)" vs the list's bare "Silver Surfer".
- **Marvel Wolverine "first of five":** the Wolverine – Blue & Yellow premium statue was billed as *first of five* — no evidence the other 4 dropped. **Re-check** whether they ever materialized.
- **Marvel × Funko Iron Man (2023):** a physical-redemption product with an undisclosed digital twin — deliberately **not catalogued** (data not published). Revisit if VeVe ever lists the digital editions.
- **Star Wars craft-damaged helmets** (Stabbed/Cut/Gouged): `comic_debut` set to the classic Stormtrooper (A New Hope, 1977) — change to blank if you prefer "damaged variant" items carry no first-appearance.
- **Free-to-craft items** (Beskar Ingots, Bambi bases, Piston Cup, Mos Espa Grand Arena, Peter Parker craft): `drop_price_gems: 0` reflects the $0 list price. Confirm that convention.

## 5. Reserve-count nuance (affects low-mint / MCP)

`lowest_public_mint` is the **first edition available to the public** (`#1–N` reserved by VeVe). Standard older drops reserve 40 → first public **#41**, but **2024–2026 lower-edition drops reserve fewer** (verified per item): **#21** (20 reserved), **#16**, **#11**, **#6**. These are read from the blog, not assumed — but worth spot-checking, since the MCP low-mint bonus depends on the public pool size. See [[Master Collector Points]] · [[Significant Mints]].

## 6. Already resolved (logged for the record)

- ✅ **Tsuburaya → Tsuburaya Productions** — normalized across all 13 Ultraman collectibles (frontmatter + body).
- ✅ **Rabbids** — confirmed correctly filed under the `rabbids` universe (an earlier mis-file under `assassins-creed` is no longer present).
- ✅ **`type: comic-issue` → `collectible`** — renamed everywhere in a prior pass.

## How to mark something done

After verifying an item: correct the field(s), set `updated:` to today, and bump `confidence: "high"`. For a domain, fill `licensor`/`parent` and remove the `> [!warning] Licensor flag` callout. Re-run the catalog export (`/tmp/export_catalog.sh`) so the app picks up changes.

## See also

- [[lint-report-2026-06-25]] — structural health (orphans, frontmatter gaps)
- [[collectibles-verified-data]] — provenance / data sourcing
- [[conventions]] — frontmatter + linking rules

nft/azuki.md:
# Azuki

## Overview

Azuki is a collection of 10,000 anime-styled avatar (PFP) NFTs on Ethereum, created by Los Angeles-based startup Chiru Labs and launched on January 12, 2022. The public sale used a Dutch auction starting at 1 ETH (set to decay 0.05 ETH every 20 minutes toward 0.15 ETH), but the 8,700 publicly offered tokens sold out in roughly four minutes at the full 1 ETH price, grossing about $29 million before the first price reduction could trigger; remaining supply went to a whitelist sale and the team. Holders gain membership in "The Garden," the project's community and brand universe, signified by a red bean motif.

Chiru Labs was founded by four pseudonymous builders — Zagabond (CEO, described as a former big-tech entrepreneur), 2pm.flow (CTO), location tba (engineer) and HoshiBoy (CPO) — with Arnold Tsang (alias Steamboy), a former Overwatch character artist, as art director. The ecosystem grew through the BEANZ companion collection (~19,900 tokens airdropped free to holders on March 31, 2022) and the Elementals collection (June 27, 2023), a 20,000-piece expansion that raised about $38 million in 15 minutes but triggered a community revolt because the artwork closely resembled the originals; Azuki's floor fell roughly 44% in the aftermath.

Each Azuki is generated from 12 trait categories (Type, Hair, Clothing, Eyes, Mouth, Offhand, Background, Ear, Face, Headgear, Neck, Special) spanning roughly 450 attribute values. The four Type tiers dominate valuation: Human (~90.2%), Blue (~4.4%), Red (~4.4%) and Spirit — only 97 exist. In 2024–2025 the project pivoted toward an "on-chain anime" strategy, launching AnimeChain (an Arbitrum-based L2) and the ANIME token on January 23, 2025, with 37.5% of the 10 billion supply allocated to the Azuki community.

## Cultural significance

Azuki became the defining anime-aesthetic NFT brand of the 2021–22 cycle, briefly rivaling Bored Ape Yacht Club in floor price and establishing that a non-Western art style could anchor a blue-chip collection. Its history is marked by sharp swings driven by its own team: in May 2022 founder Zagabond's blog post "A Builder's Journey" revealed he had abandoned three earlier NFT projects (CryptoPhunks, Tendies, CryptoZunks), roughly halving the floor from ~19–21 ETH to ~10–11 ETH in a day; in June 2023 the Elementals mint raised ~$38M in 15 minutes but the near-identical artwork was seen as diluting the brand, cutting Azuki's floor ~44%. The project also contributed the open Physical Backed Token (PBT) standard, demonstrated with its October 2022 golden-skateboard auction, and pivoted into anime media infrastructure with AnimeChain (Arbitrum L2) and the ANIME token (January 23, 2025, 37.5% of supply to the Azuki community) — an attempt to convert a PFP collection into an "open anime" entertainment ecosystem. No celebrity ownership claims could be verified for this page.

## Traits

| Trait category | Distinct values |
|---|--:|
| Type | 4 |
| Hair | 123 |
| Clothing | 98 |
| Offhand | 53 |
| Headgear | 36 |
| Ear | 32 |
| Mouth | 30 |
| Eyes | 27 |
| Face | 19 |
| Neck | 15 |
| Special | 9 |
| Background | 8 |

**Famous rare traits:**

- **Spirit (Type)** (97) — Rarest of the four Type tiers (0.97%); Spirits average far above collection floor and include the record-sale pieces. Other tiers: Human ~90.18%, Blue ~4.44%, Red ~4.41%.
- **Golden Cat Kigurumi (Clothing)** (5) — Rarest of the golden kigurumi series (cat, sloth, red panda, frog); the single scarcest documented clothing trait.
- **Golden Zanbato (Offhand)** (11) — Rarest golden offhand weapon; other golden offhands: Golden Sheathed Katana (12), Golden Monkey King Staff (12), Golden Katana (12).

# Bitcoin Puppets

## Overview

Bitcoin Puppets is a 10,001-piece profile-picture (PFP) collection inscribed on Bitcoin via the Ordinals protocol. The mint went live on January 3, 2024 on the inscription service InscribeNow (inscribenow.io) as a free mint (minters paid network/inscription fees) and minted out quickly, with some suspected bot activity. The images are deliberately crude, hand-drawn MS Paint monkey-like puppet characters — the collection is famously self-described with the meme that it was 'hand-drawn in MS Paint by a 12-year-old' — and the project explicitly offers 'no roadmap, no promises': the official site describes the work as pure art created 'with basic tools, lots of effort and passion.'

The creator is a pseudonymous, deliberately undoxxed artist known as Le Puppeteer Fou (X/Twitter: @lepuppeteerfou), also called 'The Puppeteer' or 'The Puppetmaster.' Before Bitcoin Puppets he created Lasogette, a 7,777-piece generative 'net-art' PFP collection on Ethereum, and O.P.I.U.M. (Ord Puppet Inu Undoxxed Millionaires), a 777-piece hand-drawn puppet collection free-minted on Bitcoin Ordinals on March 25, 2023, which is widely considered the direct predecessor of Bitcoin Puppets. The founding community traces back to friendships formed in the Wassies by Wassies Discord during the Ethereum NFT era, and community members contributed directly to trait design in both O.P.I.U.M. (submitting the text on puppets' signs) and Bitcoin Puppets.

The collection is released under the Viral Public License (VPL), a CC0-like copyleft that predates CC0-style NFT licensing and permits anyone to make derivatives and merchandise; the artist simultaneously holds a firm 'No-Collab Thesis' refusing official collaborations. Notable sub-groups include the 'Cursed Puppets' (a set of 21 glitched/fringe inscriptions listed by number on the official site) and the separately tracked 'Bitcoin Puppets Honoraries,' an ever-growing set of 1-of-1 puppets the artist creates as tributes to figures such as Ordinals creator Casey Rodarmor, DeeZe, ThreadGuy, and Ansem.

Market-wise, the collection's floor hit a then-record 0.178 BTC (~$11,141) on February 29, 2024 per Magic Eden data, then surged during the spring 2024 Ordinals run: on April 12, 2024 the floor reached ~0.46 BTC, and on April 22, 2024 (nftnow's publication date) it sat at 0.408 BTC (~$26,775), with the collection coming close to flipping NodeMonkes by market cap and floor around April 8, 2024. Weekly volume spiked again in late 2024 ($3.03M in one September 2024 week per crypto.news). The unaffiliated but community-adopted $PUPS memecoin ecosystem (BRC-20, bridged to Solana, migrated to Runes as PUPS•WORLD•PEACE at the April 2024 halving) rewarded Puppet holders via the Rune Pups airdrop of March 17, 2024. As of mid-2026, CoinGecko shows the floor around 0.0102 BTC (~$660-820) with roughly 6,021 holders across 10,001 items.

## Cultural significance

Bitcoin Puppets became the definitive anti-establishment statement of the 2024 Ordinals wave. Where Ethereum PFP projects sold polished art, roadmaps, and 'utility,' the Puppets offered deliberately ugly MS Paint scrawl, a manifesto titled 'The Gospel of World Peace,' a middle-finger cursor easter egg on the official website, and the ironic community rallying cry 'send them to zero' — a rejection of floor-price obsession that reframed financial nihilism as community glue. The polarizing art was itself the filter: mockery from outsiders ('FUDders') only strengthened the cult, and holders flooded X/Twitter timelines with puppet imagery and world-peace messaging, making the puppet a recognizable meme persona of Bitcoin-native counterculture and, alongside NodeMonkes, the face of Ordinals' challenge to Ethereum blue chips (whose floors, like BAYC's, were collapsing at the same moment).

The trait lore is genuinely community-authored: the 'two chairs' t-shirt trait evolved from a community member's riff on Michael Saylor's 'how many chairs are you sitting on?' Bitcoin rhetoric (with a red/blue Matrix-pill twist by the artist), the 'pink pipe' references BennyTheDev's PIPE protocol ('trac pipe' joke), and the 'Coffee Time' mug immortalizes a community member's misprinted merchandise order. The VPL license spawned a large derivative ecosystem (Le Puppettes and many others), music albums, merch, and IRL meetups at ETH Denver, NFT.NYC, and Bitcoin 2024 Nashville — all without any official collaboration, by design.

## Traits

**Famous rare traits:**

- **Two Chairs t-shirt (shirt)** (?) — Community-lore trait from a member's riff on Michael Saylor's 'how many chairs are you sitting on?' all-in-on-Bitcoin rhetoric; the artist colored the chairs red and blue as a Matrix pill reference
- **Pink Pipe (accessory)** (?) — References BennyTheDev's PIPE protocol, nicknamed 'trac pipe' in overlapping Discord circles
- **Coffee Time mug (accessory)** (?) — Born from community member Hillshills receiving a misprinted 'Coffee Time' mug instead of 'Rise and Grind' — a lore-canonized accident
- **Cursed Puppet (variant)** (21) — The official site's 'Cursed Puppets' section lists 21 specific inscriptions by number; polarizing glitched/fringe aesthetic beloved by part of the community

## Market snapshot

Live data on the [Market page](../../app/market.html) (cross-platform tab). As of 2026-08-03: floor **$662**, marketcap **$6,619,110** (floor-based), 6,021 holders.

## Links

- Marketplace: https://magiceden.io/ordinals/marketplace/bitcoin-puppets

> - The name 'LeoCrypto' as creator could not be confirmed in any source; every credible source attributes the collection to the pseudonymous Le Puppeteer Fou — treat 'LeoCrypto' as incorrect

# Bored Ape Yacht Club

## Overview

Bored Ape Yacht Club (BAYC) is a collection of 10,000 procedurally generated profile-picture NFTs depicting cartoon apes, minted as ERC-721 tokens on Ethereum (contract 0xBC4CA0EdA7647A8aB7C2061c2E118A18a936f13D). It launched in late April 2021 at a mint price of 0.08 ETH (~$190) and sold out within about 12 hours. The collection's fiction casts each ape as a member of a swamp-side club for apes grown "bored" after crypto wealth; the token itself functions as a membership card, originally gating perks such as a collaborative-graffiti "bathroom." Unusually for the era, Yuga Labs granted holders commercial-use rights to their individual ape images, which enabled holder-run brands, music projects, and merchandise.

BAYC was created by Yuga Labs, founded in early 2021 by writers Greg Solano ("Gargamel") and Wylie Aronow ("Gordon Goner") together with engineers Zeshan Ali ("No Sass") and Kerem Atalay ("Emperor Tomato Ketchup"); the founders operated pseudonymously until their identities were made public in February 2022. The lead artist on the collection was the Asian-American illustrator known as All Seeing Seneca. Each ape is assembled from seven trait categories (background, fur, eyes, mouth, hat, clothes, earring) drawn from a pool the project describes as over 170 possible traits, with 4 to 7 traits per ape; trait scarcity drives large price differences between individual apes.

BAYC became the defining "PFP" collection of the 2021–22 NFT cycle. Its floor price peaked around 128 ETH (~$354,000) in May 2022, when Yuga Labs was valued at roughly $4 billion and had expanded the ecosystem with companion collections, the ApeCoin token (March 16, 2022), the acquisition of the CryptoPunks and Meebits IP from Larva Labs (March 2022), and the Otherside metaverse project (launched April 30, 2022, with Animoca Brands). In the subsequent bear market the floor fell roughly 90%, to about 13.4 ETH (~$40,000) by May 2024. Cumulative BAYC trading volume has exceeded $1 billion.

## Cultural significance

BAYC became the mainstream face of the 2021–22 NFT boom and, later, of its bust. Celebrity owners included Justin Bieber, Eminem, Snoop Dogg, Paris Hilton, Jimmy Fallon, Gwyneth Paltrow, and Stephen Curry, and Eminem and Snoop Dogg performed as their apes in the 2022 "From the D 2 the LBC" music video; Adidas bought an ape in 2021 ahead of its metaverse push. Sotheby's legitimized the collection in traditional auction circles with the $24.39M "Ape In!" lot (September 2021) and the record $3.4M sale of #8817 (October 2021). Yuga Labs leveraged the brand into ApeCoin, the Otherside metaverse, and ownership of CryptoPunks and Meebits, reaching a ~$4B valuation in 2022. The project also drew the era's backlash: an SEC investigation opened in October 2022, a class-action suit filed in December 2022 (dismissed September 2025), phishing/theft incidents against holders, copycat collections, and a ~90% floor-price collapse by 2024 — making BAYC a standard case study in both NFT cultural adoption and speculative excess.

# Claynosaurz

## Overview

Claynosaurz is a collection of 3D-animated, claymation-style dinosaur NFTs on Solana, created by a studio of animation-industry veterans. The core mint of 10,000 characters went live on November 26, 2022 and sold out (co-founder Nicholas Cabana says the launch "sold out and crashed the website" and raised about $1.3 million; trackers such as Moon.ly and Bitget News report a mint price of 10 SOL). A burn mechanic later expanded the genesis collection: 222 'Sardinha' items could be burned with a Claymaker into Giant Eggs that hatched into Dactyls, bringing the flagship collection to 10,222 characters across 7 species (Ankylo, Bronto, Dactyl, Raptor, Rex, Stego, Trice), per the official GitBook. A separate 2,000-piece expansion, 'Claynosaurz: The Call of Saga' (species Para and Spino, 1,000 each), was announced in April 2023 exclusively for Solana Mobile Saga phone users; it is its own collection and should not be conflated with the 10,222 genesis supply. Aggregators vary slightly on supply (HowRare indexes 10,000 core items; CryptoSlam shows 10,002; CoinGecko lists 10,232).

The studio was founded in late 2021 by animators Nicholas Cabana and Daniel Cabral, who serve as co-chief creative officers. Cabana started at Sony Animation & Imageworks and worked in VFX/creature animation at MPC, Image Engine, Rodeo FX and Framestore, with credits on Jurassic World, Paddington 2, Fantastic Beasts, X-Men: Days of Future Past and Suicide Squad (Annie Award nomination), plus animation-supervisor work on Game of Thrones and His Dark Materials. Cabral is a Brazilian animator who originally created the Claynosaurz characters for his son. The wider team draws artists from Illumination, DreamWorks, Sony, Framestore, Disney, Ubisoft, Netflix and others; Andrew Pelekis (CFA, formerly a director at Innovatus Capital Partners) is CEO, per the official docs and IQ.wiki.

Every Claynosaurz NFT is a fully animated 3D character rather than a static image — motion is literally a trait (walk cycles such as Gallop, Trot, Run and Idle), reflecting the founders' pitch that blockchain lets animators own and monetize 'a walk cycle, a gesture, an expression.' The brand positions itself as a community-owned transmedia IP: viral animated shorts on social media, large fan events (Lisbon, Los Angeles, New York, Paris, Annecy presence), a Gameloft mobile-game partnership announced September 12, 2024 (choose-your-own-adventure plus location-based mechanics), a merchandise shop, an expansion onto Sui with the 25,000-piece 'Popkins' collection, and in July 2026 the release of its first three animated micro-episodes (characters Flea, Bex, Trix and Milo in the world 'Claynotopia') on Amazon Prime Video, also available on Apple TV.

The trait system (verified via the HowRare index of the 10,000-item core collection) spans Species, Skin (10 values, rarest 'Apres' at 281), Color (8, rarest 'Mist' at 388), Motion (6, rarest 'Run' at 693), Mood (8), Background (6), Class (6: Warrior, Mystic, Stalker, Defender, Tracker, Mender), layer/on-off traits, and 14 one-of-one 'Ancients' — six golden 'Midas' dinos (one per species) plus eight named characters (Trevor, Travis, Trish, Tristan, Tyson, Tom, Tiffany, and 'Toly, Toby And Tony'). The official docs count 22 Ancients in total: 18 across the genesis collection (including Dactyl Ancients) and 4 in The Call of Saga. CoinGecko records an all-time-high floor of 97 SOL (April 3, 2023) and $5,843.88 (December 19, 2024); CryptoSlam's all-time top sale is Ancient Midas Bronto (#8755) at 537.5 SOL (~$116,139).

## Cultural significance

Claynosaurz became one of the defining NFT brands of the post-2022 'NFT winter,' proving a Solana collection could grow while most PFP projects faded. Its soft, toy-like claymation aesthetic deliberately reads as mainstream family entertainment rather than crypto-native PFP culture, and the team framed the mint itself as a crowdfunding mechanism for an artist-owned IP — a story the animation trade press (Animation Magazine, AWN) has covered as a creator-economy success case, with Cabana keynoting the 2025 World Animation Summit and speaking at the VIEW Conference. The project claims over 40 industry awards for its animated content and built an audience of hundreds of thousands across social platforms through viral shorts.

Within the Solana ecosystem it functions as something of a mascot IP: the Call of Saga expansion was the flagship perk for Solana Mobile's Saga phone, an Ancient is named 'Toly, Toby And Tony,' and news events (the Gameloft deal in September 2024, the Amazon Prime Video debut in July 2026) repeatedly sent its floor price to the top of Solana NFT rankings — by July 2026 its market cap (~$19–20M) briefly surpassed Ethereum blue chips Milady Maker and Azuki. Its trajectory from NFT mint to Prime Video micro-series, mobile games and plush merchandise is frequently cited as the template for 'NFT-to-IP' brand building.

## Traits

| Trait category | Distinct values |
|---|--:|
| Species | 6 in core 10k (Rex 2,135 / Trice 1,900 / Stego 1,700 / Ankylo 1,600 / Bronto 1,400 / Raptor 1,251); 7 incl. Dactyl |
| Skin | 10 |
| Color | 8 |
| Motion (animation cycle) | 6 |
| Mood | 8 |
| Background | 6 |
| Class | 6 |
| Layer count | 5 |
| Back / Belly / Pattern / Details | 2 each (On/Off) |
| Ancient (1/1s) | 14 in core 10k; 22 across all collections per official docs |

**Famous rare traits:**

# CloneX

## Overview

CLONE X — X TAKASHI MURAKAMI (commonly "CloneX") is a collection of 20,000 algorithmically generated 3D avatar NFTs on Ethereum, created by digital-fashion studio RTFKT with Japanese contemporary artist Takashi Murakami. Unlike flat PFP projects, each Clone was conceived as a metaverse-ready identity: holders received fully rigged 3D character files usable in games, AR filters, and virtual environments, and Murakami contributed signature motifs (flowers, smiley mouths, "drip" elements) as generative traits. Rarity is anchored by eight "DNA" types, from Human (50%) down to Alien (0.15%).

The launch ran in late November 2021: a presale of 11,133 tokens for existing RTFKT NFT holders at 0.05 ETH opened November 27, with the public sale (2 ETH, initially structured as a Dutch auction from 3 ETH) planned for November 29 but delayed a day after RTFKT's site buckled under demand and bot attacks; the collection nonetheless sold out. Two weeks later, on December 13, 2021, Nike acquired RTFKT — terms undisclosed — instantly making CloneX the centerpiece of Nike's web3 strategy and cementing its blue-chip status through 2022, when floor prices peaked in the high teens of ETH.

The project's later arc is a cautionary tale. Nike announced in December 2024 that it would wind down RTFKT operations by end of January 2025. On April 24, 2025, CloneX and Animus artwork briefly went dark across marketplaces after Cloudflare downgraded RTFKT's account, displaying a "content restricted" notice; former RTFKT tech lead Samuel Cardillo subsequently migrated the artwork to the permanent-storage network Arweave. In parallel, a class action filed in 2025 sought over $5 million from Nike, characterizing the RTFKT shutdown as a "soft rug pull." Co-founder Benoit Pagotto died in October 2025 at age 41.

## Cultural significance

CloneX marked Takashi Murakami's full entry into NFTs and became the template for fashion-brand web3 plays: Nike's December 13, 2021 acquisition of RTFKT — two weeks after mint — was read industry-wide as legacy fashion's endorsement of digital collectibles, and CloneX avatars anchored Nike/RTFKT's subsequent ecosystem (MNLTH/Cryptokicks sneaker NFTs, physical "forging" of apparel, CloneX Chains jewelry with Crown Collection). The collection crossed into the traditional art world in May 2022 when Gagosian's "An Arrow through History" (976/980 Madison Avenue, New York — Murakami's first solo New York show at the gallery since 2014) exhibited paintings and sculptures based on CloneX alongside the gallery's first VR experience, built with RTFKT and Oncyber. The collection is also cited for inclusivity in generative design (e.g., vitiligo skin variants). Its decline — Nike's December 2024 wind-down of RTFKT, the April 2025 Cloudflare outage that temporarily blanked the artwork (prompting migration to Arweave), and a class action calling the shutdown a "soft rug pull" — made CloneX a reference case in debates over corporate custodianship of NFT projects and off-chain asset fragility.

## Traits

| DNA | 8 |
| Hair | 163 |
| Clothing | 119 |
| Mouth | 49 |

| Eye Color | 33 |

**Famous rare traits:**

- **Alien DNA** (0.15% (= 30 of 20,000)) — Rarest DNA type; despite scarcity, Aliens have not commanded the collection's top sales — the priciest early Alien sale was 88.88 ETH (Dec 2021)
- **Murakami DNA** (0.5% (= 100 of 20,000)) — Fully Murakami-designed clones; the most coveted DNA in practice — the record 450 ETH sale (#4594) was a Murakami DNA clone. Also counted among the Murakami Drip traits
- **Undead DNA** (0.6% (= 120 of 20,000)) — Third-rarest DNA type
- **Reptile DNA** (1.25% (= 250 of 20,000)) — Fourth-rarest DNA type
- **Murakami Drip traits** (39 distinct traits) — Traits designed by Takashi Murakami (eyes, mouths, helmets, outfits); roughly 15% of all clones carry at least one Murakami Drip trait

# Cool Cats

## Overview

Cool Cats is a collection of 9,999 randomly generated ERC-721 profile-picture (PFP) NFTs on Ethereum, each depicting "Blue Cat" — a cartoon character created by artist Colin Egan (Clon) roughly a decade before the drop (Animoca Brands dates the character to 2013). The collection launched on July 1, 2021 at a mint price of 0.06 ETH; after a slow first hour the team cut the price to 0.02 ETH (refunding early minters the difference), and the collection sold out within about eight hours. Each cat is assembled from four trait categories — body, hat, face, and shirt/outfit — drawn from a pool the team described as offering over 300,000 possible combinations.

Rarity is governed by a points-based "coolness" system: every trait carries points, and each cat's total (3–10 points) places it in one of four bands — Cool (3–4 pts, 4,599 cats), Wild (5–6 pts, 3,000), Classy (7–8 pts, 1,750) and Exotic (9–10 pts, ~650) — each split into two sub-tiers (cool_1 through exotic_2). Cool Cats became one of the archetypal "blue-chip" PFP collections of the 2021 NFT boom, following the CryptoPunks/Bored Ape playbook of a fixed-supply avatar set with community-driven value, and later expanded into a gamified ecosystem ("Cooltopia") with an ERC-20 token (MILK) and a 19,999-piece companion collection, Cool Pets (February 2022).

By 2025 the collection had generated over US$410 million in lifetime trading volume, ranking around 19th among all NFT collections by lifetime sales, and in August 2025 Animoca Brands and Coin Operated Group completed a strategic investment giving them a majority stake in Cool Cats Group.

## Cultural significance

Cool Cats' cultural breakout came days after launch, when Mike Tyson set a Cool Cat as his Twitter profile picture (about eight days post-mint), an endorsement widely credited with accelerating the collection's rise; Steve Aoki is also a documented holder, and NFTevening additionally names Reese Witherspoon, Marc Benioff, Alexis Ohanian and Puma among buyers. The project partnered with TIME magazine in 2021, signed with Hollywood talent agency CAA in March 2022 for representation across licensing and media, and on November 23, 2023 became the first NFT collection featured in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, with a balloon of Blue Cat and his milk-carton companion Chugs seen by an estimated 28.5 million viewers. Alongside CryptoPunks, Bored Apes, Doodles and Pudgy Penguins, Cool Cats is regularly cited as one of the definitive PFP collections of the 2021 cycle; its ecosystem expanded with the MILK token and Cooltopia gamified economy and the Cool Pets companion drop (19,999 NFTs, February 2022). After the 2022 downturn the collection's floor fell far below its roughly 14–19 ETH late-2021/early-2022 peak, and in August 2025 Animoca Brands and Coin Operated Group took a majority stake in Cool Cats Group, citing over $410M in lifetime volume.

## Traits

| Body | 1 (all gen-1 cats share the Blue Cat Skin body, per the community wiki) |
| Face | ~56 listed values (community wiki listing; incl. Zombie, Mummy, Ditto, Three Eyes) |
| Hat | ~99 listed values (community wiki listing) |
| Shirt / Outfit | ~104 listed values (community wiki listing) |
| Tier (derived from points) | 8 (cool_1, cool_2, wild_1, wild_2, classy_1, classy_2, exotic_1, exotic_2) |

**Famous rare traits:**

- **Hidden 1/1 cats** (9) — Nine one-of-one cats secretly created by Clon and xtremetom without telling the rest of the team (per OpenSea's own description); they include the zombie Cool Cat #1490 and the robot-themed Cool Cat #3330, and account for three of the collection's four highest early sales
- **Exotic tier (9–10 points)** (~650) — Top coolness band; sources give 649–650 of 9,999
- **Exotic 2 sub-tier** (<150) — The rarer half of the Exotic band — fewer than 150 cats of 9,999
- **'Super rare' cats** (66) — 66 cats cited as super/ultra-rare, one step below the nine 1/1s
- **Tier distribution (context)** (4,599 / 3,000 / 1,750 / ~650) — Cool (3–4 pts) / Wild (5–6) / Classy (7–8) / Exotic (9–10) — sums to 9,999

# CryptoPunks

## Overview

CryptoPunks is a collection of 10,000 algorithmically generated 24x24-pixel characters on Ethereum, released by the two-person studio Larva Labs in June 2017. It is one of the earliest non-fungible token projects on Ethereum and predates the ERC-721 standard, which it is credited with inspiring; the collection uses its own custom contract with a built-in marketplace. The artwork draws on the London punk scene, the cyberpunk movement, and Daft Punk. At launch the punks were free to claim (gas only); claiming was slow for the first week until a June 2017 Mashable article, after which the remaining supply was claimed within about a day. Larva Labs' founders claimed 1,000 punks for themselves before the public release.

The original 2017 contract contained a marketplace bug that let a buyer reclaim the ETH they had paid, so Larva Labs deployed a fixed contract on June 23, 2017 and re-issued all 10,000 punks to their existing owners; this "V2" contract (0xb47e3cd837dDF8e4c57F05d70Ab865de6e193BBB) is the canonical collection today, while the abandoned V1 tokens later resurfaced as a separate wrapped collection. Each punk is one of five types — 6,039 Male, 3,840 Female, 88 Zombie, 24 Ape, and 9 Alien — and carries zero to seven of 87 possible accessories (hats, hair, glasses, beards, etc.). Rarity is driven by type, by scarce accessories, and by unusual attribute counts.

Ownership of the IP has changed hands twice: Yuga Labs (creator of Bored Ape Yacht Club) acquired the CryptoPunks and Meebits IP from Larva Labs on March 11, 2022 and granted commercial rights to individual holders; in May 2025 Yuga Labs sold the CryptoPunks IP to the nonprofit Infinite Node Foundation (NODE), which stewards the collection and runs museum-placement programs.

## Cultural significance

CryptoPunks is widely treated as the archetype of NFT collectibles: an inspiration for the ERC-721 standard, a catalyst of the 2021 NFT boom, and the profile-picture status symbol of that era. Visa bought CryptoPunk #7610 for 49.5 ETH (~$150,000) in August 2021, a purchase credited with triggering a record sales run, and celebrity owners have included Jay-Z, Serena Williams (a gift from husband Alexis Ohanian), and other high-profile figures. Punks were the first NFTs sold in marquee evening sales at both Christie's ($16.96M for nine punks, May 2021) and Sotheby's ($11.75M for #7523, June 2021). Through the Punks Legacy Project, punks entered permanent museum collections — #305 at the ICA Miami (December 2022) and #110 at the Centre Pompidou in Paris (February 2023) — and Wikipedia records MoMA adding ten CryptoPunks in December 2025. The infamous October 2021 "sale" of punk #9998 for $532M was a flash-loan self-purchase and is excluded from legitimate sale records.

## Traits

| Type (species) | 5 |
| Accessories / attributes | 87 |
| Attribute count per punk (0-7) | 8 |

**Famous rare traits:**

- **Alien** (9) — Rarest type; aliens account for most of the top all-time sales (#5822, #7804, #3100, #7523)
- **Ape** (24) — Second-rarest type (e.g. #4156, sold for 2,500 ETH in Dec 2021)
- **Zombie** (88) — Third-rarest type
- **Beanie** (44) — Rarest accessory in the collection
- **7 attributes** (1) — Only one punk has the maximum seven accessories (widely identified as #8348, which stacks Big Beard, Buck Teeth, and more)
- **0 attributes** (8) — Only eight punks have no accessories at all; a distinct rarity niche

# DeGods

## Overview

DeGods is a 10,000-piece profile-picture (PFP) NFT collection depicting "degenerate" deities in modern streetwear, launched on the Solana blockchain on October 8, 2021 at a mint price of 3 SOL (~$450). The mint sold out in seconds — largely to bots due to a technical error — and early missteps briefly earned the project rug-pull accusations before it recovered to become the highest-valued NFT collection on Solana. Its early design included the "Paper Hands Bitch Tax," a 33.3% penalty on sales below the floor price; 535 DeGods were burned under this mechanism, cutting supply to roughly 9,465.

The project built an ecosystem around the collection: the $DUST staking token (33.3M max supply), the DeadGods art upgrade (March 2022, unlocked by burning 1,000 $DUST), the 15,000-piece sister collection y00ts (September 2022), and the DeDAO treasury/governance arm. In December 2022 the team announced it was leaving Solana; DeGods migrated to Ethereum in April 2023 (contract 0x8821bee2ba0df28761afff119d66390d594cd280), while y00ts moved to Polygon under a $3M grant and then to Ethereum in 2023–24, returning the grant. In February–March 2023 the 535 burned DeGods were re-inscribed on Bitcoin via the Ordinals protocol — all in a single block, #776408 — making DeGods one of the first major brands present on Solana, Ethereum, and Bitcoin.

The collection was created by Rohun Vora, known as "Frank" (frankdegods), through the Los Angeles studio De Labs (which merged with Dust Labs; Kevin Henrikson was co-founder). The August 2023 "Season III" update — a self-described "art downgrade" — triggered a community backlash that halved the floor price within days. Vora stepped down as CEO on May 12, 2025, handing leadership to community members @0x_chill and @pastagotsauce.

## Cultural significance

DeGods is the defining Solana NFT success story and one of Web3's best-known comeback narratives: pre-mint hype built on the provocative 33.3% "Paper Hands Bitch Tax," a botched bot-dominated mint, near-collapse in late 2021, then a 2022 run to the top of the Solana market (monthly volume grew from ~$375K in Dec 2021 to $25M+ in April 2022) powered by the DeadGods deflationary art upgrade and $DUST staking. In April 2022 its DAO made mainstream headlines as the first NFT community to buy into a professional sports team, paying ~$625,000 (via 25 Fire-Tier BIG3 NFTs) for ownership of the Killer 3s in Ice Cube's BIG3 league — Ice Cube himself bought DeGod #3177 for 265 SOL (~$26,500). The project's serial chain-hopping (Solana → Ethereum, y00ts to Polygon and back, 535 burned pieces inscribed in a single Bitcoin block) made it a bellwether for multi-chain NFT strategy, while the August 2023 Season III "art downgrade" — which halved the floor within days — became a cautionary tale about altering PFP art. Founder Rohun Vora ("Frank"), one of the most-followed and most-scrutinized figures in NFTs, denied insider-trading allegations and retired from the project on May 12, 2025.

# Doodles

## Overview

Doodles is a collection of 10,000 generative profile-picture (PFP) NFTs on Ethereum, launched on October 17, 2021 at a mint price of 0.123 ETH. The art — pastel-toned line characters including humans, cats, aliens, apes, pickles and skeletons — was created by Canadian illustrator Scott Martin, known as Burnt Toast. The collection sold out quickly and its floor price climbed to 2.3 ETH within the launch month; current supply is tracked at 9,998 items.

The founding team paired Martin's art with two NFT-industry veterans: Evan Keast ("Tulip") and Jordan Castro ("Poopie"), both formerly of Dapper Labs, where they worked on CryptoKitties. The launch was notable for its community strategy — the pre-mint Discord was closed at an early member cap, with existing members receiving mint access — and for DoodleBank, a community treasury (later reported above $5 million) through which holders vote on proposals. Trait rarity was augmented by 62 fully hand-drawn "Custom" Doodles by Martin, the collection's closest analogue to CryptoPunks' Aliens or BAYC's solid-gold fur.

Doodles became one of the cycle's "blue chip" PFP collections and then deliberately repositioned as a media/consumer brand. Extensions include Space Doodles (February 2022, a reversible wrapper placing each Doodle in an animated spaceship) and the Dooplicator (May 2022, a device for generating wearables tied to Doodles 2). Pharrell Williams joined as Chief Brand Officer in June 2022, and in September 2022 the company raised $54 million at a $704 million valuation, led by Alexis Ohanian's Seven Seven Six with FTX Ventures, Acrew Capital and 10T Holdings. In 2023 a co-founder publicly stated Doodles was "no longer an NFT project"; later milestones include a McDonald's McCafé holiday-cup collaboration (November 2024) and the launch of the DOOD token on Solana (May 9, 2025, 10 billion supply with roughly 30% airdropped to the community).

## Cultural significance

Doodles is regularly grouped with CryptoPunks, Bored Ape Yacht Club and Pudgy Penguins among the definitive 2021-cycle PFP collections, distinguished by Burnt Toast's pastel aesthetic and an early community-treasury governance model (DoodleBank). Celebrity holders reported in the press include Steve Aoki (who bought the second-most-expensive Doodle) and Snoop Dogg, with DJ Timmy Trumpet also cited as an owner. Pharrell Williams' appointment as Chief Brand Officer in June 2022 signalled a push into music and entertainment, followed by the $54 million Seven Seven Six-led raise at a $704 million valuation in September 2022. The brand's stated pivot away from being purely an NFT project (a co-founder told CoinDesk in March 2023 it was "no longer an NFT project") drew both mainstream partnerships — most visibly the November 2024 McDonald's McCafé holiday-cup collaboration, which drove a sharp floor-price and volume rebound — and criticism from crypto-native collectors. In 2025 the brand launched the DOOD token on Solana (10 billion supply, ~30% community airdrop), which more than doubled NFT sales volume around launch.

# Mad Lads

## Overview

Mad Lads is a 10,000-piece profile-picture collection on Solana — roughly 9,000 male "Lads" and 1,000 female "Lassies" — drawn by artist Yann Penno in a style commonly described as anime-meets-Peaky-Blinders. It was created by Coral (later rebranded Backpack), the developer of the Anchor framework and the Backpack wallet, led by Armani Ferrante and Tristan Yver. Mad Lads was the first collection of "xNFTs" (executable NFTs): tokens carrying embedded code that runs as a native app inside the Backpack wallet, enabling token-gated chats, staking for soulbound "gold," collection locking, and direct-to-wallet claims.

The launch became part of the collection's lore. Madlist (allowlist) claims opened February 28, 2023; the mint was announced April 11 and priced at 6.9 SOL. The April 20, 2023 public mint was hit by DDoS attacks, extortion threats, and hundreds of thousands of bogus bot transactions, forcing a 24-hour postponement. On the April 21 relaunch the team routed humans to the real mint and bots to a decoy "honeypot" mint contract, which trapped roughly $250,000 in SOL from bots — refunded within 24 hours. The collection sold out, and within days secondary trading records fell: a peak of about $8.2 million in 24-hour volume, nearly triple Bored Ape Yacht Club's over the same span, with Solana's daily NFT volume exceeding 50% of Ethereum's for the first time. Artwork was revealed through a built-in game in which holders collectively "defeated" the Mad King inside their NFTs.

Arriving months after the FTX collapse and weeks after DeGods and y00ts left Solana, Mad Lads is widely credited with reviving the Solana NFT market — Ferrante described the moment as the space needing "a new heartbeat." The floor peaked at 229.425 SOL (~$16,000) in early December 2023 amid Backpack Exchange early-access perks; lifetime secondary volume passed $200 million (≈3.51M SOL through 2024), making it Solana's leading collection by market cap and volume for extended periods.

## Cultural significance

Mad Lads is credited with restoring confidence in Solana NFTs at the ecosystem's lowest point — post-FTX and immediately after DeGods/y00ts migrated away — and with proving the xNFT concept of NFTs as executable apps. In its first days it out-traded every Solana and Ethereum collection, and in April 2023 a Mad Lads trading incentive briefly let Tensor flip Magic Eden in Solana marketplace volume. Holding a Lad became a yield position: holders got first-wave access to Backpack Exchange (November 2023) and the collection became the most-airdropped on Solana, receiving allocations from Pyth Network, Wormhole, Dymension, and dozens of other projects, which drove the December 2023 floor peak above 200 SOL. Community identity centers on the mottos "WAO" (We Are One) and "Fock It," global meetups (Tokyo, Seoul, Manila, Istanbul, Vietnam, and elsewhere), a sponsored extreme-sports "Roster," a Solana Mobile partnership engraving Lads onto Saga devices, and honorary 1/1s awarded to public figures — Iggy Azalea (an honorary Lassie, dubbed "Mother" by the community), Haliey "Hawk Tuah" Welch, and Meltem Demirors. Solana co-founder Anatoly Yakovenko publicly endorsed the launch, calling xNFTs a distribution bridge to mass consumer audiences.

# Meebits

## Overview

Meebits is a collection of 20,000 procedurally generated 3D voxel-style avatars on Ethereum (ERC-721), created by Larva Labs — the two-person studio behind CryptoPunks and Autoglyphs. Announced and launched on May 3, 2021, Meebits was pitched as the 3D successor to CryptoPunks: low-poly characters in the Minecraft/Roblox visual tradition, intended for use as avatars in "virtual worlds, games, and VR." Each owner can download an asset pack including the full 3D model and a T-pose OBJ file for rigging and animation, and the project shipped with a built-in zero-fee marketplace supporting ETH sales and multi-item Meebit-for-Meebit trades signed off-chain.

Distribution split the supply in two: roughly 11,000 Meebits were reserved as free claims (gas only) for CryptoPunks and Autoglyphs owners during a 7-day community grant, while the remaining ~9,000 were sold via Dutch auction starting at ~2.5 ETH. The public sale sold out within hours, grossing on the order of $70–80 million (~22,500 ETH). Launch day also produced one of the NFT era's best-known exploits: because trait data had leaked via IPFS, an attacker wrote a contract that repeatedly "rerolled" mints — reverting any transaction that didn't yield a rare ID — and landed Meebit #16647, an ultra-rare Visitor, which collector Pranksy bought for 200 ETH (~$700,000). Larva Labs briefly paused minting in response.

In March 2022, Yuga Labs (Bored Ape Yacht Club) acquired the Meebits and CryptoPunks IP from Larva Labs — along with 1,711 Meebits held by the studio — and extended full commercial rights to individual holders. In February 2025, Yuga sold the Meebits IP onward to The Meebit Company (MeebCo), a firm backed by venture fund 1confirmation and led by Sergio Silva, which announced a "Bits" participation-rewards system and an OpenSea marketplace partnership.

## Cultural significance

Meebits carries cultural weight primarily through lineage: it was Larva Labs' third project and the designated 3D heir to CryptoPunks, launched at the peak of 2021 NFT mania with the then-novel "free claim for holders of the ancestor collection" model that many later projects copied. It became an early flagship of the metaverse-avatar thesis (owner-downloadable, riggable 3D models), and its launch-day reroll exploit remains a canonical case study in NFT smart-contract security. The collection was also the poster child of the January 2022 LooksRare wash-trading episode (~$4.4B in fake Meebits volume), a defining event in NFT market-data skepticism. Its IP odyssey tracks the industry's consolidation arc: Larva Labs → Yuga Labs (March 2022, with commercial rights granted to holders) → The Meebit Company/MeebCo (February 2025, backed by 1confirmation). Prices never sustained CryptoPunks-level demand — MeebCo's CEO called the avatars "very ahead of their time" — but the collection remains one of the most historically significant profile-picture projects on Ethereum.

# Milady Maker

## Overview

Milady Maker is a collection of 10,000 generative ERC-721 profile-picture NFTs on Ethereum, created by Remilia Corporation (also styled Remilia Collective) and launched on August 25, 2021. The avatars are drawn in a self-described "neochibi" anime style inspired by Y2K Tokyo street-fashion tribes; every Milady is procedurally assembled from cosmetics themed around five style "cores" — Gyaru, Prep, Lolita, Hypebeast, and Harajuku (with 15 core combinations in the metadata). The mint used tiered pricing that discounted bulk purchases, and the collection took roughly eight months to mint out, completing on April 19, 2022 — a slow start for what later became one of the most traded PFP collections on Ethereum. The artwork is copylefted under the Viral Public License.

Milady Maker's signature mechanic is the "drip score": instead of ranking purely by trait scarcity, each cosmetic is scored on rarity weighted by the prominence of its slot, with bonus points for matching hat/shirt themes ("costume complete" badges). Every token carries an on-chain-referenced Drip Score (observed range 12–67) and a letter Drip Grade from Normal/C/B/A/S up to SS (533 of 10,000 are SS-drip). The project frames this as valuing stylistic coherence over raw rarity. Direction is credited to Charlotte Fang (Remilia's founder, widely reported to be Krishna Okhandiar), with the visual style executed by a digital painter credited in Remilia's design notes as Milady Sonora (site credits list Yuyu, Sprite, and Charlotte Fang as artists).

The collection's trajectory has been unusually volatile even by NFT standards: a founder scandal in May 2022 cut the floor by more than half, an Elon Musk meme tweet in May 2023 roughly doubled it within hours, and Vitalik Buterin's adoption of a Milady profile picture in January 2025 triggered another major rally. Through these swings Milady became the anchor of a sprawling ecosystem — derivative collections (Redacted Remilio Babies, Bonkler, community-made Pixelady), memecoins (LADYS, the Milady Cult Coin/CULT), and an internet-subculture identity ("network spirituality") that has kept it culturally prominent well past the 2021 PFP cycle.

## Cultural significance

Milady Maker is as famous for its subculture as for its art. In May 2022, DefiLlama developer 0xngmi linked founder Charlotte Fang to the pseudonymous "Miya" account, which had posted racist and homophobic content and been tied to an alleged online "suicide cult"; Fang admitted to running the account, apologized, and announced departure from the team — the floor fell over 55% to roughly $454 — though Fang later described the exit as "performative" and resumed open leadership, recasting Miya as collaborative satirical performance art under Remilia's "post-authorship" doctrine. The collection rebounded into an unlikely blue chip: on May 10–11, 2023 Elon Musk tweeted a Milady meme captioned "There is no meme. I love you," sending the floor from ~3.75 ETH to over 7 ETH within hours and the unaffiliated LADYS memecoin up over 5,000%; in January 2025 Vitalik Buterin bought Milady #9286 (5.82 ETH) and made it his profile picture, driving another ~40%+ floor surge. Around the collection grew the "network spirituality" aesthetic movement, official derivatives (Redacted Remilio Babies, Bonkler), community spin-offs (Pixelady), and the CULT token (December 2024), whose presale reportedly raised $20 million in six hours — making Milady one of the few 2021-vintage PFP projects to remain culturally central through 2026.
