# What Drives the Value of a VeVe Collectible?

Collectors usually answer this with the rarity tier, and the rarity tier is the *weakest* of the big drivers. Ranked against **302,286 real completed market sales** (2025-07-12 → 2026-07-30, ~$9.15M of volume, both markets normalised to USD), the order is roughly **surviving supply → subject/franchise demand → rarity tier → mint number**, with **liquidity** acting as a discount on all four. This page separates what the sale data supports from what it can only suggest, and it repeatedly returns to one correction: **the headline prices you have seen are outliers, not the level.**

For the mechanics of tiers, editions and reserves see [[platform/rarity-system]]; this page is about price.

## The short answer

| Driver | Direction | Strength in the sale data | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Surviving / circulating supply** | fewer = dearer | Spearman **ρ = −0.68** vs median sale price; holds inside every tier | High — measured |
| **Franchise / universe** | blue-chip = dearer, and far more liquid | Top-5 universes = **70%** of dollar volume; universe medians span **$5–$87** | High — measured |
| **Rarity tier** | higher = dearer | Median item price **$4.00 Common → $50.00 Secret Rare**, but ranges overlap heavily | High — measured, effect modest |
| **Subject within an identical set** | fan-favourite = dearer | Median spread only **1.33×** with supply, rarity and set held fixed | Medium — n = 160 groups |
| **Mint number** | low / significant = dearer | **3.61×** median premium in the *ask* book; realised premium **not measurable here** | Medium for asks, unverified for sales |
| **First appearance / key issue** | key = dearer | No comic sale data in this vault — external evidence only | Low — external only |
| **Liquidity** | thin = discount | Median item trades **~4×/month**; 49% of traded items change hands less than weekly | High — measured |
| **Sealed vs opened** | n/a | No sealed-box asset and no condition axis exists on VeVe | High — structurally absent |
| **Original drop price** | *not* a driver | **80.9%** of items trade **below** their drop price | High — measured |

## 1. Surviving supply is the strongest single driver

Not the edition size printed on the item — the number that actually still exists and is in public hands. Across 2,554 collectibles with at least one recorded sale, ranked by circulating supply against the item's own median sale price:

| Circulating supply | Items | Median sale price |
|---|---:|---:|
| under 100 | 204 | **$203.76** |
| 100 – 500 | 528 | $40.00 |
| 500 – 1,000 | 534 | $14.11 |
| 1,000 – 2,500 | 689 | $7.22 |
| 2,500 – 5,000 | 296 | $5.88 |
| 5,000 – 10,000 | 210 | $3.20 |
| 10,000 + | 93 | $2.99 |

Perfectly monotone, and it is not an artefact of rarity tiers riding along with supply — the relationship survives when you hold the tier constant (ρ = −0.59 within Common, −0.63 within Secret Rare):

| Circulating supply | Secret Rare median | Common median |
|---|---:|---:|
| under 100 | **$196.00** *(n=95)* | — |
| under 500 | — | **$210.47** *(n=106)* |
| 100 – 300 | $75.00 *(n=204)* | — |
| 300 – 1,000 | $35.00 *(n=247)* | — |
| 500 – 2,000 | — | $3.32 *(n=139)* |
| 1,000 – 3,000 | $17.25 *(n=82)* | — |
| 2,000 – 5,000 | — | $3.00 *(n=97)* |
| 3,000 + | $10.06 *(n=12)* | — |
| 5,000 + | — | $2.45 *(n=131)* |

**A sub-500 Common ($210 median) out-trades a 3,000+ Secret Rare ($10 median) by 21×.** Concretely: *Michelangelo - Classic (Special Edition)* is a **Common** with 77 in circulation and a $1,337 median sale, while *The Lion King Pencil* is a **Secret Rare** with 3,419 in circulation and an $8.00 median.

Because ~12% of all issued supply has been **burnt** and a further slice sits unsold in the store, the printed edition size is often the wrong number entirely — [[platform/rarity-system]] §6–7 walks the four supply figures and which one to use.

## 2. Franchise and universe demand

Demand is heavily concentrated. Star Wars and Marvel alone are **36.6% of all recorded sales**, and the top five universes are **70% of dollar volume** — but sale *count* and *price* are different things, and the split between them is where franchise demand actually shows up.

| Universe | Sales | Share of $ volume | Items | Median item price |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| star-wars | 53,300 | 19.4% | 217 | $17.49 |
| marvel | 57,227 | 18.8% | 418 | $10.99 |
| disney | 26,136 | 12.5% | 221 | $13.39 |
| dc | 14,785 | 12.3% | 78 | $12.99 |
| veve (house brand) | 12,154 | 7.0% | 83 | $20.00 |
| real-world-brand | 38,952 | 5.7% | 321 | $8.00 |
| tmnt | 12,979 | 4.4% | 23 | $9.98 |
| veve-vibes | 20,767 | 3.8% | 334 | $13.00 |
| street-fighter | 2,625 | 2.3% | 18 | **$44.00** |
| avatar-the-last-airbender | 3,100 | 1.3% | 9 | **$87.30** |
| solo-leveling | 2,030 | 1.2% | 6 | **$59.99** |

Two readings worth separating. **DC turns over 4.9% of sales into 12.3% of volume** — a small, expensive catalog (78 items). And the highest per-item medians on the board belong to *small* licences with intense fandoms (Avatar at $87, Solo Leveling at $60, Street Fighter at $44), which is scarcity of *catalog* as much as demand: nine Avatar items serve an entire fanbase, while 418 Marvel items compete with each other.

**Within** a franchise, the specific subject matters much less than collectors assume. Holding set, rarity tier *and* edition size identical — so only the character differs — the highest-to-lowest median price ratio across 160 such groups is only **1.33× at the median**, 1.87× at the 75th percentile, 2.94× at the 90th. Example: the *Star Wars Holiday Posters* Ultra Rares (978 editions each) run $20.00 down to $6.80. Real, but a 2× effect, not a 10× one.

> [!warning] Unverified
> The catalog's `character` field is derived, not authoritative, and it mis-groups (e.g. "Death Trooper" props collapse into a "Death" character). Per-character price tables built on it are unreliable, which is why this page reasons at universe level and within identical sets instead.

## 3. Rarity tier — real, but the weakest of the headline drivers

| Tier | Items with sales | Median item price | Median of all sales |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Common | 473 | $4.00 | $3.49 |
| Uncommon | 360 | $4.50 | $3.50 |
| Rare | 508 | $6.99 | $6.00 |
| Ultra Rare | 570 | $14.98 | $13.99 |
| Secret Rare | 640 | **$50.00** | $33.00 |

A 12.5× spread from Common to Secret Rare — meaningful, and far less than the 68× spread you get from supply alone. Note also that **Common and Uncommon are effectively the same price** ($4.00 vs $4.50), mirroring their near-identical edition sizes. And the tiers overlap enormously in both directions: the highest sale in the entire window is a Secret Rare (*Melvin*, $44,999) and the sixth-highest is a **Common** (*Stormtrooper*, $11,204).

Tier's hardest mechanical effect is not price at all — it is [[Master Collector Points|MCP]] yield, where Secret Rare pays 6.00/day against a Common's 1.00. Tier is a *points* multiplier that happens to correlate with price.

## 4. Mint number: a large ask premium, an unmeasured sale premium

This is where the honest answer diverges most sharply from the folklore. VeVe reserves a block of low editions (usually #1–40) so the lowest buyable mint is typically **#41** — see [[platform/rarity-system]] §5 — and collectors pay up for low mints, #1s, ceiling mints, palindromes, meme numbers and character-meaningful years, catalogued in [[Significant Mints]].

Measured on the **live ask book** (19,199 VeVe listings, snapshot 2026-07-30), across 941 items that have both sub-100 asks and ordinary-mint asks:

| Percentile | median(sub-100 ask) ÷ median(other ask) |
|---|---:|
| 25th | 1.82× |
| **50th** | **3.61×** |
| 75th | 9.12× |
| 90th | 37.0× |

**72.4% of those items ask at least 2× for a sub-100 mint; 8.5% ask less.** The upper tail is not a market signal — it is troll pricing on illiquid items (the 99th percentile is >35,000×, which no one pays).

> [!warning] Unverified — realised mint premium
> **This vault's sale mirror records the collectible, date and price, but not the mint number that sold.** So the premium above is what sellers *ask*, not what buyers *pay*, and the true realised low-mint premium cannot be computed here. The widely-circulated multiples — sub-100 at 10× / 8× / 6× / 4× / 3× floor for Common → Secret Rare, and sub-50 at 20–30× — come from one community analysis (a Randy Chavez marketplace survey, via Vevepedia) and are **not independently confirmed by this dataset**. Treat them as directional folklore.

## 5. First appearances and key issues

For comics, first-appearance status is a real and central selection criterion: VeVe's app catalog is deliberately weighted toward keys, and this vault holds **309 comic records flagged as containing a first appearance out of 3,984**. GoCollect describes the app's comics as "typically historical & first appearance titles, established as keys or grails by the comic book collecting community," and notes collectors specifically target edition numbers that reference a character's first-appearance year.

That mint-number-as-tribute behaviour ties directly back to §4 — a first appearance creates a *set of meaningful numbers* (Batman's #1939, Spider-Man's #1962) that trade above their neighbours.

> [!warning] Unverified — no comic price data
> **All 302,286 sales in this vault's mirror map to collectible (figure/art) records; there are no comic sales in it.** Any statement here about how much a first appearance is worth on VeVe is external evidence about the *comic market in general*, not a measurement of VeVe pricing. The premium is asserted, not quantified. `# TODO` — ingest comic market sales.

## 6. Sealed vs opened — a driver that structurally does not exist here

In physical collecting, sealed/graded condition is often the single largest value multiplier. On VeVe it is absent in both directions:

- **There is no sealed blind box to trade.** VeVe's [[Blind Box|blind box]] format assigns you a random collectible from the set at purchase — "you won't know which collectible you get until after payment," per VeVe's own series pages — and what lands in your collection is an already-revealed item. There is no unopened box asset that can be held, flipped, or sold blind. The catalog's `blind` flag marks *items that came from a blind-box drop* (1,539 of them), not sealed boxes; items whose names contain "Box" are packaging-themed artwork, not containers.
- **There is no condition or grade.** A digital collectible does not wear, and reading a digital comic does not degrade it — VeVe's own pitch is enjoying an issue "without risking a single crease or fingerprint." Two copies of the same item at the same mint number are identical.

The practical consequence: **every value axis on VeVe is set at drop time or by supply changes afterward.** Nothing you do to your copy makes it better or worse.

## 7. Liquidity — the discount on everything above

A price you cannot transact at is not a value. The catalog is far thinner than its headline sale count suggests:

| Liquidity measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Median sales per item over the 12.6-month window | **53** (~4.2/month) |
| 10th-percentile item | 10 sales in 12.6 months |
| Items with fewer than 12 sales in the window | 322 (12.6%) |
| Items trading less than weekly (<52 sales) | 1,250 (48.9%) |
| Items with **zero** recorded sales | 160 |
| Items with **no live ask on either market** | 203 |
| Median VeVe ask-book depth per item | 6 listings |
| Median StackR ask-book depth per item | 3 listings |

Nearly half the catalog trades less than once a week, and a six-listing order book means one seller moves "the floor." Illiquidity is also why the highest *asks* are unreliable: on a thin book, a single fantasy price becomes the visible number.

The two markets do not agree, either. Of 2,050 items with live asks on both venues, **StackR's lowest ask is cheaper 70.5% of the time** (median ratio 0.83 of the VeVe ask, converting StackR's OMI-denominated asks at $0.0001528/OMI) — so "the price" depends on which venue you look at. Fees then take a further bite: VeVe states secondary-market fees are shown at listing time and "may vary between Collectibles," and does not publish a single rate (the exact percentage remains `# TODO` in [[platform/omi-economics]]).

## 8. Two things that do *not* drive value

**The original drop price.** Of 1,338 items with a known drop price and at least five sales since 2026-05-01, the median item trades at **0.38× its drop price**. **80.9% trade below drop price; 60.3% trade below half of it.** Only 10.6% trade above 2×, and 2.2% above 10×. Buying at drop is not a value driver — it is, for four items in five, a markdown.

**Age.** Median item price by [[platform/drops|drop]] season runs $9.00 (S1), $6.50 (S2), $5.24 (S3) … $24.45 (S10), $16.00 (S11). Older is not dearer. Some of that rise is simply higher drop prices in later seasons, so read this only as a rejection of "vintage = valuable," not as evidence that new is better.

## 9. The distribution — why headline sales mislead

Almost everything on VeVe is cheap, and almost all the money is in a sliver of sales:

| Percentile of all 302,286 sales | Price |
|---|---:|
| 25th | $2.11 |
| **50th (median)** | **$5.94** |
| 75th | $15.55 |
| 90th | $48.60 |
| 95th | $102.22 |
| 99th | $420.25 |
| 99.9th | $2,000 |
| max | $44,999 |

**65.0% of sales are under $10; 94.8% are under $100.** The mean, $30.26, is five times the median. **The top 1% of sales carry 37.3% of all dollar volume; the top 5% carry 62.8%.**

Per item, the gap between the record and the level is enormous — the median item's highest sale is **4.3× its own median**, and at the 90th percentile it is **45.8×**. The four items collectors quote most:

| Collectible | Tier | Circ. | Sales | Median | 90th pct | 99th pct | **Record** |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| [[deadbeats-series-one-melvin\|Melvin]] | Secret Rare | 4,999 | 144 | $9.00 | $11.20 | $29.00 | **$44,999** |
| [[stormtrooper-rotj\|Stormtrooper]] | Common | 15,010 | 1,094 | $9.00 | $13.98 | $55.00 | **$11,204** |
| [[leonardo-classic-2026-01-03\|Leonardo - Classic]] | Common | 2,937 | 1,678 | $9.98 | $17.94 | $198.51 | **$7,576** |
| [[avatar-aang-aang-airbender\|Aang - Airbender]] | Common | 1,955 | 2,019 | $19.18 | $31.99 | $95.96 | **$5,758** |

Melvin is the cleanest case in the vault: **the single highest sale ever recorded here, $44,999, sits on an item whose ordinary copies change hands for $9.** That $44,999 was almost certainly a specific mint, a specific moment, or both. It is a real sale — see [[platform/record-sales]] — and it is not the value of a Melvin.

## 10. So how should you value a copy?

1. **Start from the item's real median sale price**, not its floor. Across 2,212 liquid items (≥12 sales) carrying a live ask, the **lowest ask across both venues sits 1.22× the median real sale** at the median, and **68.1% of items have a lowest ask above their own median sale**; 14.8% are above 2×. A floor is a *lowest-ask listing*, not a traded value — [[platform/floor-prices]].
2. **Adjust for supply**, using circulating (post-burn, post-reserve) supply, not the printed edition.
3. **Adjust for liquidity.** Under ~12 sales a year, there is no reliable price at all; say "unknown," not a number.
4. **Treat any mint premium as a hypothesis.** It is well-evidenced in asks, unmeasured in sales.
5. **Never value a collection off record sales.** They are the 99.99th percentile of a distribution whose median is $5.94.

> [!note] Method
> All figures are computed from this vault's own mirrors, snapshot **2026-07-30**: `tools/market_sales_cache.jsonl` (302,286 completed sales, 2025-07-12 → 2026-07-30, both markets normalised to USD, per-collectible with no mint number), `app/data/catalog.js` (2,849 catalog records; 2,714 carry the token id used to join sales) and `app/data/all_listings.js` (19,199 live VeVe asks + 8,524 StackR asks, as of 09:40 UTC 2026-07-30). "Median item price" throughout means the median across items of each item's own median sale price, which prevents high-volume items from dominating. "Circulating supply" means the catalog's `circ` field, falling back to `issued` then `edition` for the 187 traded items that carry no `circ` value — this is what makes the §1 buckets sum to all 2,554 traded items. StackR asks are OMI-denominated and converted at `omiUsd` = $0.0001528 (`app/data/floor.js`, corroborated against public OMI quotes of ~$0.00015 on 2026-07-30); comparisons that skip this conversion overstate VeVe-side floors. Percentile thresholds use nearest-rank. Aggregates only — no holder, wallet or account data is used or published.

> [!warning] Data caveats
> - The sale window opens **2025-07-12**; the legendary pre-window sales collectors cite are not in it.
> - The mirror contains **no comic sales** and **no mint numbers**, which caps §4 and §5 at "unverified."
> - Venue is not recorded per sale, so VeVe-vs-StackR realised prices cannot be split here (only their ask books can be compared).
> - Everything above is **descriptive of this snapshot**. It is not a forecast, and it is not investment advice.

## Sources

- https://www.veve.me/blog/news/how-the-veve-nft-marketplace-works/
- https://www.veve.me/veve-fees
- https://www.vevepedia.com/terms/low-mint/
- https://www.vevepedia.com/terms/blind-box/
- https://www.veve.me/collectibles/en/series/bf93ad0c-f519-4cfd-8280-0233d5d6e1d9
- https://www.veve.me/blog/comics/the-benefits-of-digital-comics/
- https://gocollect.com/blog/embracing-the-digital-revolution-veve-comics-the-future-of-comic-collecting
- Internal: `tools/market_sales_cache.jsonl` — 302,286 completed market sales, 2025-07-12 → 2026-07-30
- Internal: `app/data/catalog.js` + `app/data/all_listings.js` — catalog and live ask-book snapshots, 2026-07-30
- Internal: [[platform/rarity-system]] · [[platform/record-sales]] · [[platform/floor-prices]] · [[Significant Mints]]

# VeVe Catalog, Rarity & Drop Mechanics

Research synthesis (2026-06-24). Mechanics are well-documented; the exhaustive brand list is login-gated and the area of most uncertainty.

## Collectible Types *(high)*
- **Digital Collectibles** (Premium) — 3D rendered, AR-viewable. The flagship format. Rarity + edition numbers apply.
- **Digital Comics** (since 2024) — *readable* licensed comics, incl. same-day-as-print (Marvel); limited editions + variant covers. Both media and collectible.
- **Digital Art** — premium editioned artwork from named artists.

## Rarity Tiers (official, common → rare) *(high)*
**Common · Uncommon · Rare · Ultra Rare · Secret Rare (SR).**
- Not every drop has all five; some have 1–2.
- Rarity ≠ strict edition size; SR editions vary widely (sometimes <100, sometimes >1,000).
- Each copy has a unique **mint/edition number** (e.g. "#100 of 5,000").

## Mint Numbers / "Low Mint" *(medium — community-sourced)*
- Lower mint numbers = scarcer = priced higher.
- VeVe holds back allocation for licensors/marketing → **lowest available public mint is often #41**.
- Community-observed sub-100 premiums over floor: Common ~10×, Uncommon ~8×, Rare ~6×, Ultra Rare ~4×, SR ~3×; sub-50 ≈ 20–30×. *(directional, fluctuates)*

## Drop Mechanics *(high)*
- **Drop** = timed release (store/primary); **Market** = secondary resale (fixed price + auctions).
- **Single-item drop** vs **Blind Box** (random item, rarity/edition unknown until after purchase; used to seed Secret Rares; better odds due to larger pool).
- **Waitlist/Queue:** opens **12h before**, closes **5 min before**; random allocation; **KYC users prioritized**; winners get a **5-min** purchase window; leftovers hit the store ~**7 min** after the drop. No need to pre-load Gems.

## Brand / Licensor Catalog
VeVe cites **"50+ licensors"**; the "200+ brands" figure counts sub-franchises/artist lines. Full in-app list is **login-gated** (`veve.me/brands`, `veve.me/collectibles/...`). Best exhaustive target: `ecomiwiki.com/veve/collectibles/licensors/latest` (needs headless browser).

**Confirmed brands** (beyond the obvious Marvel/DC/Disney/Pixar/Star Wars/Star Trek):
Ghostbusters, Back to the Future, Jurassic Park/World, James Bond 007 (MGM), RoboCop (MGM), Rambo/Studiocanal, Alien, Predator, Avatar (Cameron), Labyrinth/Jim Henson, The Boys, The Little Prince, Tarzan (ERB), Sesame Street, TMNT, Ren & Stimpy, Cartoon Network, Adventure Time, Powerpuff Girls, Astro Boy, Ultraman (Tsuburaya/VIZ), VIZ Media, Avatar: TLA, Solo Leveling, Street Fighter/Capcom, Rabbids/Assassin's Creed/Ubisoft, Lamborghini, Maserati, Coca-Cola, USPS, Funko, Givenchy, Christian Louboutin, Cryptozoic (Cryptkins), FiGPiN, ElmonX, Mondo, Toy Tokyo, The London Police, Breadcat, Ducobi, DesignerCon, BLACKPINK (YG), Stan Lee (Kartoon), and artists (Ron English, Patrick Hughes, Tristan Eaton, Matt Gondek, Frank Kozik, Jermaine Rogers, Scott Tolleson, Bigshot Toyworks).

> [!warning] Catalog corrections to my earlier skeleton
> - **tokidoki** — appears in marketing/AR copy but **no confirmed licensor deal found** → mark uncertain, not confirmed.
> - **Voltron, Knight Rider, Chucky** — **not surfaced** in this research → treat as unverified until confirmed against an official source.
> - **NFL/NFLPA** — FORMER license (lapsed). **Chaosium / Call of Cthulhu** — DISCONTINUED (2022).
> - **Pokémon, Hasbro (Transformers/G.I. Joe/MOTU), Sanrio, SEGA** — **NOT present** (no source).

## Notable Facts
- Company founded **2018** as ECOMI (Auckland NZ); rebranding to **Collect** (2025–26). *(high)*
- Largest mobile NFT platform Q4 2021 (~744k installs, ~$112.5M spend, SensorTower). *(medium)*
- Apr 2024 (likely stale): >$150M collectibles market cap; Marvel >1.28M collectibles issued, Disney >600k; top-10 licensors ≈ 75% of market cap. *(medium, dated)*
- Milestones: first Marvel Spider-Man NFT (Aug 2021), USPS stamps (Nov 2021), Lamborghini Huracán (Feb 2023), VeVe Comics (2024), BLACKPINK/YG (May 2024). *(high)*

## Sources
- https://www.veve.me/brands · https://www.veve.me/blog/veve/veve-101/go-to-market
- https://www.veve.me/blog/veve/101/veve-waitlist-drops-what-you-need-to-know/

# VeVe Collectibles — Verified Per-Item Data

Research synthesis (2026-06-24): real, cited data for a starter set of 24 iconic VeVe **Premium Collectibles**. Feeds [[collectibles/_index|the catalog]].

## The authoritative per-item source (the bulk-fill pipeline)

**`https://www.veve.me/blog/collectibles/<slug>`** is the official, authoritative page per collectible — it reliably lists exact **drop date/time, edition size per variant, rarity, list price in Gems, the per-item reserved count, and the "First Available Public Edition" number.** *(high)*
- Pre-2023 drops live on `medium.com/veve-collectibles`.
- Secondary floor / live lowest-available-mint: `ecomiwiki.com/veve/collectibles/...` and `ecomiwiki.com/veve/market` (the app itself is auth-gated, not scrapable).
- Full set lists: `vevesetlist.com/sets`.

This means the full catalog (thousands) is **systematically ingestible** per-item — the starter set below proves the pipeline.

## Field reliability
- **First-appearance dates, licensor, character → HIGH** (public record).
- **Drop date, edition size, rarity, list price → HIGH** for any item with a live veve.me/blog or Medium page (most rows).
- **Lowest public mint:** community/official rule = #1–40 reserved → **#41 lowest public** (vevepedia.com/terms/mint-number), but **item-specific** — confirmed exceptions: **Marvel Metallic Red** series list **#21** (only ~40–55 reserved); **Venom** confirmed #41 (90 reserved). Treat "~#41" as policy default to verify per item.
- **Known gaps (marked ❓ / # TODO, not guessed):** #100 Todd McFarlane Batman drop price (early 2020 drop, undocumented); Iron Man (Jul 2023) rarity; Thor First Appearance & Thor Metallic Red rest on search-summaries — re-fetch their blog pages before treating as fully verified.

## Data table
See [[collectibles/_index|the live catalog table]] for all 24 rows (name, universe, license, rarity, edition, drop price, lowest mint, drop date, first appearance). Each collectible has its own page with a per-item confidence note.

## Primary sources (fetched/verified)
- veve.me/blog/collectibles/: spider-man-marvel-metallic-red, marvel-iron-man-marvel-metallic-red, marvel-venom, dc-batman-black-and-white-series-7, star-wars-return-of-the-jedi-luke-skywalker-character-series, spider-man-2099, marvel-wolverine, marvel-hulk-animated
- medium.com/veve-collectibles: modern-marvel-series-1, marvel-1sts-captain-america-series-1, superman-series-1, star-wars-darth-vader, star-wars-underworlders-collection-boba-fett, dc-artists-alley-series-1, modern-marvel-series-2-throg

# VeVe / Collect Data Landscape & APIs

Research synthesis (2026-06-24) on what data is obtainable for building the community app. Confidence + source per claim.

## Key Claims

- **No official public VeVe / Collect / StackR developer API or docs exist.** The app uses a private backend; using it is against ToS. *(high)*
- **`collectscan.com` is the official Collect Chain block explorer, running Blockscout, with a fully public unauthenticated JSON REST API** (`/api/v2/...`). This is the primary data source for **holders, transfers, ownership, and edition instances.** *(high — verified live)*
- **VeVe NFTs are one ERC-721 contract on Collect Chain:** `0xbcFEbA7A9dA14f5C9453bDA72E2098537867B3c7`, ~705,100 holders. *(high)*
- **Floor prices, USD value, and drop dates are NOT on-chain** and have no official API. This is the hardest data gap. Options: third-party (Veve Alpha, EcomiWiki), partner data, or self-maintained scraping (fragile, ToS-grey). *(high)*
- **A user's holdings are queryable by WALLET ADDRESS via collectscan, no login.** Querying by **VeVe username is NOT publicly possible** (mapping is private). Users must paste their Collect Chain wallet address. *(high)*
- **No third-party NFT API (NFTScan, Bitquery, CoinGecko) covers Collect Chain.** *(high)*

## Verified collectscan endpoints (`https://collectscan.com`)

| Endpoint | Returns |
|----------|---------|
| `GET /api/v2/stats` | chain stats |
| `GET /api/v2/tokens?type=ERC-721` | token list (VeVe contract, holders_count) |
| `GET /api/v2/tokens/{address}` | contract metadata (`total_supply` returned **null**) |
| `GET /api/v2/tokens/{address}/holders` | **holder distribution** (paginated, address + balance) |
| `GET /api/v2/addresses/{address}/nft?type=ERC-721` | NFTs held by an address |
| `GET /api/v2/tokens/{address}/instances` | per-edition/serial metadata *(standard Blockscout — verify before relying)* |
| `GET /api/v2/tokens/{address}/transfers` | transfer history *(verify)* |

## NFT instance metadata schema (verified 2026-06-24, live)
`GET /api/v2/addresses/{addr}/nft?type=ERC-721` and `/tokens/{contract}/instances` return per-edition items whose `metadata` carries everything needed for the app:
`name, rarity (Common…Secret Rare), edition (= mint number), totalEditions (= edition size), comicNumber, series, characters[], publisher, dropDate, mintDate, startYear, image, artists/writers/coverArtists`. Comic vs collectible ⇒ `comicNumber` present = comic.
- **CORS is open** (`access-control-allow-origin: *`) → the browser can call it directly; **no proxy needed for the prototype.** *(verified)*
- **Wired into the app** (`app/assets/collectscan.js`): MCP Optimizer + Mint Checker now run on **live holdings by wallet address** (tested: a wallet returned 1,500 editions → 1,622 MCP/day, 310 significant mints).

> [!warning] Caveats
> - collectscan is a **third-party public service** with undocumented rate limits / no SLA. Cache hard, low concurrency, never a hard single point of failure. *(high it works now; low on documented limits)*
> - The `/holders` response showed `token_id: null` with aggregate per-address balances — per-serial ownership likely needs `/instances` + `/transfers` reconstruction. **Verify `/instances` indexes per-edition metadata before designing around it.** *(medium)*
> - Public **RPC URL + chain ID for Collect Chain were not found** — pull from collectscan's network UI. *(medium)*

## Blockchain history
GoChain (2021) → Immutable X (Dec 2021, Ethereum L2) → **Collect Chain** (VeVe's own EVM chain; full migration ~early/Apr 2026). Self-custody "Phase 2" announced, **not yet shipped**. *(high on sequence; medium on exact migration date)*

## Third-party tools
- **Veve Alpha** (vevealpha.com) — floor/listing alerts, mint tracking, VeVe+StackR arbitrage; **no public API**; freemium. *(high)*
- **EcomiWiki** (ecomiwiki.com) — market/floor data, licensor DB (`/veve/collectibles/licensors/latest`, JS-rendered). Best target for the full brand list via headless browser. *(medium)*
- **Vevepedia** (vevepedia.com) — glossary/education only. *(high)*

## Sources
- collectscan.com (live API) · https://docs.blockscout.com/devs/apis/rest
- https://www.veve.me/blog/veve/updates/veve-completes-full-migration-on-collect-chain/
- https://vevealpha.com/ · https://ecomiwiki.com/veve/market · https://www.vevepedia.com/
- https://medium.com/veve-collectibles/veve-welcomes-immutable-x-807097d57057

# VeVe Economy — Gems, OMI & Master Collector Points

Research synthesis (2026-06-24). Most MCP values are **officially published verbatim** on `veve.me/blog/veve/mcp/*` — unusually, the formula is public.

## Gems
- **1 Gem = US$1.00** in-app value (ToS verbatim). *(high)*
- Bought via credit card / Apple Pay / Google Pay; VeVe recommends the web app to avoid store fees. *(high)*
- **Non-refundable, non-transferable, and (since 19 Nov 2025) non-withdrawable / non-cashable.** Closed-loop currency (compared by VeVe to Roblox/Twitch currency). The old "VeVe Payout" cash-out is gone. *(high)*
- Not a cryptoasset; not on a blockchain. *(high)*

## OMI Token
- **External settlement asset, not in-app currency.** Primary utility: **convert OMI → Gems on StackR.** *(high)*
- **$1 USD of OMI = 1 Gem**, with **7% OMI burn + 3% StackR fee** per conversion (live since 19 Nov 2025). *(high)*
- In-app items are always priced in **Gems, never OMI**. *(high)*
- Holding OMI in a linked wallet earns **bonus daily MCP points** (OMI Reward Tier, max 10M OMI eligible). *(high)*
- ⚠️ **"OMI = Collect Chain gas/native token" is UNVERIFIED speculation.** Documented OMI-gas only on Base (StackR-sponsored). *(flag)*

## Master Collector Points (MCP) — the core of the optimizer
Two parallel tracks: **Levels** (permanent, individual, total accumulated points, 0→100, exponential) and **Ranks** (dynamic, competitive percentile). MCP points are a separate currency from Gems; spending points does not lower Level/Rank.

### Daily Asset Points (drives RANK — by what you HOLD)
**Collectibles (figures):** base **1.0** each.
- Rarity bonus (added): Rare **+0.25**, Ultra Rare **+0.50**, Secret Rare **+5.00** (Common/Uncommon = base only).
- Low-mint bonus: **+0.5** (flat) for the lowest 5% of editions **available to the public** — computed on `(edition − withheld)`, **excludes any editions VeVe retained**. *(verbatim, verified 2026-06-24)*
- Duplicate diminishing (same item): 2nd **0.75**, 3rd **0.35**, 4th+ **0.10** — **applies to the 1.0 BASE ONLY.** ⚠️ **The rarity bonus (incl. +5 Secret Rare) and the +0.5 low-mint bonus are a SEPARATE "Bonus Points" section and add IN FULL to every duplicate copy** (verified 2026-06-29 across the earning-mcp page + Medium v1.0/v0.2). So a 2nd Secret Rare copy = `0.75 (base) + 5.0 (bonus) = 5.75`/day, **not** `6.0×0.75=4.5`; five identical SRs = `2.30 (base) + 5×5.0 = 27.30`/day. (Our engine previously diminished the whole value, crushing the SR bonus on duplicates — the real cause of the owner's ~4,600-vs-6,500 undercount.)

**Comics (rarity IS the base):** Common **0.25** · Uncommon **0.50** · Rare **2.0** · Ultra Rare **3.0** · Secret Rare **6.0**.
- Low-mint bonus: **+50%** (lowest 5%).
- Duplicate handling: **comic rarity value STACKS — every copy counts FULL at its rarity value (incl. Secret Rare = 6.0 each), no duplicate diminishing** (owner-confirmed 2026-06-29: "6 for comics" stacks, mirroring the collectible rarity-bonus which also stacks full per copy; a comic has no separate 1.0 base to diminish). ⚠️ This **overrides** VeVe's published comic duplicate table (which lists 2nd 50% / 3rd 25% / 4th+ 10%, Common/Uncommon exempt) per the owner's real account numbers — re-confirm against the live total; if it overshoots, partial diminishing may apply to Rare/UR/SR comic duplicates.
- **Comics do NOT earn set-completion points.** (Set Completion Points are a **collectibles-only** section in VeVe's docs — the only worked example is the collectible "Superman set"; multi-source audit 2026-06-29 found comics get no set bonus. An intermediate guess that comics earn set points was **wrong** and has been reverted — it never moved the owner's number, corroborating "no".)

**Set completion (daily, by set size):** 1→**1.0** · 2→**2.0** · 3→**3.0** · 4→**4.0** · 5+→**5.0**. Duplicate-set diminishing: 2nd **30%**, 3rd **20%**, 4th+ **10%**.

### One-Off Points
Onboarding **+100** · complete a Set **+100** (once per set ever) · Store purchase **+25** · Market purchase **+15**.

### Daily Activity Points
**+1** per in-app action (open/like/comment/share/list/buy), **capped 25/day**.

### Ranks
**22 ranks, Starter → Master Collector**; Master Collector = **top ~3%**. Dynamic — can go down if peers out-earn you. *(high)*

### Point sinks (spending MCP)
Priority Bidding (reserve a drop edition) + Store Accessories; deducted only on a winning bid. Datapoint (VeVe X, Jul 2024): a crafting event priced Ultra Rare at **250,000 MCP** and Secret Rare at **1,000,000 MCP**. *(high)*

## "Master Sets"
**Not an official VeVe term.** Official vocabulary: **"Set"** (grouping), **"Master Collector Program/Points"**, **"Master Collector"** (top rank). Set completion = **+100 one-off + Achievement Badge + daily set points**. The exact definition of "complete" (per collectible vs per rarity) is **not officially specified** — confirm in-app per set. *(high on terminology; the "all 5 rarities" claim is unverified/low)*

> [!warning] Gaps & flags
> - Exact per-Level (1–100) point thresholds are **NOT public** (shown only as an image). Do not invent. *(high it's unknown)*
> - Full list of all 22 rank names is **not published in text.** *(high)*
> - Outdated/rumor: "top 1% / 23 ranks / Bronze I" (old), "10% revenue buyback-burn" (likely superseded).
> - **Confirmed 2026-06-24:** low-mint = lowest 5% of **public** editions (excludes VeVe-retained); daily points **stop accruing after 7 days of inactivity**. VeVe's "(total editions *0.05%)" parenthetical is self-contradictory math — the "5% of public" prose governs.

## Optimization implications (for the MCP optimizer feature)
The earning math is self-documenting, so "cheapest points" is arithmetic on the values above:
1. **Secret Rares pay most per item** (SR collectible 6.0/day; SR comic 6.0/day) → cheap-floor SRs likely best points-per-gem *(formula-backed; price side needs floor data)*.
2. **Collectible duplicates are heavily penalized** (4th+ = 0.10) → breadth of UNIQUE items beats depth.
3. **Common/Uncommon comics are duplicate-exempt** → the one linear stacking path (small 0.25 each).
4. **Set completion is efficient** (+100 one-off + up to 5.0/day).
5. **Low-mint (lowest 5%)** copies get bonuses.
6. Rank is competitive & holdings-driven; Gem spend barely moves rank (+25/+15 only).
7. ⚠️ VeVe reserves the right to change MCP and prevent "gaming the system."

## Sources
- https://www.veve.me/blog/veve/mcp/veve-master-collector-program-earning-mcp-points
- https://www.veve.me/blog/veve/mcp/mcp-ranks · /mcp-levels · /...frequently-asked-questions · /...spending-mcp-points · /omi-rewards-season-one
- https://www.veve.me/terms/terms-for-gems/ · https://www.veve.me/veve-fees
- https://ecomi-official.medium.com/omi-to-gem-a-new-era-of-utility-begins-d815f7f3a757
- https://www.veve.me/blog/veve/updates/stackr-faqs/ · /omi-to-gems/
- https://x.com/veve_official/status/1809980815897485667 (MCP cost datapoint)

# Identity — Username vs Wallet

Research synthesis (2026-06-24): how a user identifies their collection in the app. **Decision: wallet-address only.**

## Key findings
- **Username → wallet address is impossible via public means.** The mapping is private to VeVe; no public resolver, API, or directory. *(high)*
- **collectscan** (the explorer) searches only by `0x` address, tx, block, or token — **no username/name resolution.** *(high)*
- **Public profiles exist** at `https://www.veve.me/en/u/<username>` (launched ~May 2026). When a user **opts in** (private by default), they expose: collectible/comic counts, set-completion stats, Collector Rank/Level, and curated **Showcases** (with mint numbers on showcased items) — but **never the wallet address** and **not a full holdings dump**. Automated/no-JS fetching is blocked (login redirect). *(high)*
- **VeVe Web Wallet** (`omi.veve.me`, login-gated) is where a user copies **their own** Collect Chain wallet address. Self-custody (Phase 2) not yet live; holdings are custodial but on-chain-visible by address. *(high)*
- Only third-party with a username↔wallet join is **VaultValue** (iOS, paid) — and it works **token → (wallet+username)** (reverse), not username → wallet. *(high)*

## Implication for the app
- The MCP Optimizer and Set Tracker need **full** holdings → require a **wallet address** (paste; user copies from `omi.veve.me`) → query collectscan. Read-only, no login, no keys.
- A username could at best deep-link to the public profile (aggregates only) — not enough to power the tools. **So: wallet-address input only** (owner's decision, 2026-06-24).

## Update — verified from the Collect data export (2026-06-26)

The owner's authoritative Collect data-warehouse docs (`documentation.zip`: `data_specification.md`, `_veve_users.md`) + a live collectscan test **resolve the open questions**:

- **The "Collect address" IS the ImmutableX wallet — same `0x`.** VeVe runs on ImmutableX; the warehouse `user` table's canonical wallet field is literally **`imx_wallet`**, `nft.owner_id` → user, and `nft.blockchain_id` = the ImmutableX token_id. **Verified:** the documented VeVe system wallets (`VeveStore` `0xc481…aFC1`, `VeveCollection` `0x7be1…2fd3`) both resolve on **collectscan** holding the VEVE token (`0xbcFE…B3c7`). ⇒ a user's **IMX wallet = their collectscan address**; there is no separate address to find. **(high, verified)**
- **Username → wallet IS resolvable — but only with warehouse access (which the owner has).** The `user` table holds `username ↔ imx_wallet ↔ profile_visible`. It's still **not publicly** resolvable (VeVe's user endpoint is auth-gated; public profiles show a showcase, not the wallet) — but the owner can **export the `user` table** (username → imx_wallet, filtered to `profile_visible`) and the app can offer a **local username search** that maps to the wallet. This supersedes the earlier "impossible" framing: impossible *publicly*, feasible *via the owner's own data*.

**Best UX for the app:** (1) paste the `0x` (= VeVe/ImmutableX wallet, from the VeVe app → Account → Wallet or `omi.veve.me`) — works today, now clarified in the input hint; (2) optional **username lookup** backed by an exported `user` table (respect `profile_visible`).

## Sources
- Collect data export: `documentation.zip/data_specification.md` (`user.imx_wallet`, `nft.owner_id/blockchain_id`), `_veve_users.md`; collectscan address API (verified 2026-06-26).
- https://www.veve.me/blog/veve/updates/new-profile-experience/ · https://www.veve.me/ve-ve-app-privacy-policy
- https://omi.veve.me · https://collectscan.com · https://apps.apple.com/us/app/vaultvalue/id1591253739

# VeVe App Update — April 2026

Summary of the VeVe app refresh (blog-dated **2026-04-16**) and the new categorisation it introduced, plus the comic-collecting **age** definitions this wiki adopted to mirror it.

## What VeVe added

From VeVe's own update posts:

- **New Collection View** with three tabs — **Collectibles**, **Comics**, **Sets**.
- **Collectibles insights:** total / unique counts, sets owned, **rarity distribution**, complete-vs-incomplete status.
- **Comics view:** reading progress ("actively reading", "unread", mark-as-finished), **comic sets**, **rarity distribution**, and a new **"comic ages"** categorisation.
- **Sets view:** sorted incomplete-first, owned-vs-needed indicators.
- Also shipped earlier in the cycle: **in-app chat**, enhanced product displays, a **rebuilt search** (fuzzy logic, better filters), **My Files** device-storage management, and **VeVe Showcase** (custom displays mixing comics/collectibles/artworks).

The blog announces **"comic ages"** as a viewable category but does **not** publish the exact year boundaries.

## How this wiki mirrored it

- **Comic ages** — every comic now carries an **Age** (by original series start year) across `app/data/comics.js`, `app/data/comic-historic.js`, the per-licensor pages in `wiki/comics/`, and the [[../comics/_ages|Comic Ages]] reference. Distribution: 🟡 Golden 12 · ⚙️ Silver 176 · 🥉 Bronze 73 · 🟤 Copper 26 · 🟦 Modern 3,532.
- **First appearances (🔑)** — VeVe's own descriptions flag first appearances / key issues; **308 comics** and **23 collectibles** are tagged (`first_appearance: true` on collectible pages; `fa` in the comic data). The [Mint Checker](../../app/mint-checker.html) surfaces a **Comics-by-age** panel + a **🔑 First appearances** section when a wallet is scanned.

### Age boundaries used

| Era | Years |
|---|---|
| ⚪ Platinum | pre-1938 |
| 🟡 Golden | 1938–1955 |
| ⚙️ Silver | 1956–1969 |
| 🥉 Bronze | 1970–1985 |
| 🟤 Copper | 1986–1991 |
| 🟦 Modern | 1992–present |

Standard collector consensus, aligned to the [League of Comic Geeks age scale](https://intercom.help/comicgeeks/en/articles/9441643-what-are-these-comic-ages) and [ScreenRant's explainer](https://screenrant.com/comics-history-golden-silver-bronze-age-explained/) (Copper 1986–1991 / Modern 1992– split).

> [!note] Confidence & caveats
> The update facts are from VeVe's official blog (high confidence). VeVe has **not** published its exact age cut-offs, so the wiki uses the standard collector boundaries above; if VeVe's in-app cut-offs differ, the single-source `tools/comic_ages.py` makes it a one-line change. Age is by **series original start year** (the only real-world-era field in the export — `original_publish_date` there is the VeVe drop date), so a late issue of a long-running classic series inherits that series' era.

## Sources

- VeVe blog — "What's New On VeVe: Comics, New Look, My Files, & More" (2026-04-16): https://www.veve.me/blog/veve/updates/whats-new-on-veve-april-2026-comics-collectibles-my-files-and-more/
- VeVe blog — "The VeVe Collection View Gets a Major Upgrade": https://www.veve.me/blog/veve/updates/new-collection-view-upgrades/
- VeVe blog — "VeVe Launches In-App Chat, Enhanced Product Displays, and Powerful New Search": https://www.veve.me/blog/veve/updates/veve-launches-in-app-chat-product-displays-and-new-search/
- League of Comic Geeks — comic ages: https://intercom.help/comicgeeks/en/articles/9441643-what-are-these-comic-ages
